Matt Willis In response to “What’s in a name” Clive Shenton’s article “What’s in a name” printed in this month’s Navigans and already received by members with an email address, has prompted a lot of response. I reprint below some of the discussion to date. “I will be sad to see the name changed as all the east coast clubs do know our club very well (even in Calais marina !!!!).... Iam proud to be a member of such a professional organisation called 'The Marconi Sailing Club' please lets keep the name as it is..” “Whilst I like the Stansgate Abbey SC there is a small problem in that it does not exist. The farmer's barn next door used to be the Clunic Priory of St Mary Magdeline which was a cell of Cluni Abbey in Burgandy. To be pedantic we should call it Stansgate Priory SC. Alternatively we could perhaps adopt the name "Stansgate SC" and distinguish ourselves from Stone SC by using the short form St. SC” “I think I would go along with Stansgate Abbey Sailing Club. I don't think the SAS connection is likely to be a serious threat to our existence and at least you can find it on a map!” “What about a twist to retain the initials 'MSC' and thus the cogitations of Marconi past (& indeed our lovely seagull logo) but use a word that reflects the club moving forward. Thus, 'My Sailing Club’. The club does belong to 'us' now, we are all individual owners, pulling together to make the club work, without the big landlord hanging over us. The name has a welcoming and personal ring to it. "My' very much reflects the ethos of the club, as it is the only club that I have come across so far that is happy to embrace all walks of sailors no matter what they sail or their level of skill without being stuffy! It keeps the known 'MSC' short name and therefore our reputation.” “The down side with doing away with the name MSC is for events such as ECPR for both MSC & ECPR are synonymous. My view is that now we will be stand alone then we should have no association with any company.” “Agree with you entirely over dropping the association with Marconi, especially as the name will be retained as an organisational entity for the foreseeable future in spite of all the recent trauma As for a name personally I favour a geographical link; particularly one as resonant as Stansgate, What about Stansgate Cruising and Sailing Club (SCSC) otherwise would be quite happy with any other Stansgate configuration.” “How about All Essex Sailing Club? People would then have an idea of where we are, and at a Stroke understand that we are not parochial. or East Anglia Scr?” Editor

MSC reaching Olympian heights?? Will a former Marconi SC member make it to the Olympic Games? Do you remember Mark Bulkeley? He might make it to the 2004 Olympics. Mark (as crew) partners Leigh McMillan (helm) in the Olympic-class Tornado catamaran and their campaign for Olympic selection has certainly met with some success this year. The Hyeres Pre-Olympic Regatta earlier this year attracted the best contestants, particularly those with Olympic aspirations as the event is often used as a ‘selection indicator' by some nations. The team of Mark and Leigh achieved a very good 8th place in the Tornado class ahead of the UK's leading team of Hugh Styles and Adam May who finished an unexpectedly lowly 18th. Mark and Leigh achieved even greater success at the Spa Olympic Regatta, coming Ist ahead of a very good field (including internationally acclaimed cat sailor Mitch Booth) with Styles and May in 8th place. Unfortunately for Mark and Leigh, the Tornado Europeans in Sardinia proved a bit of a disappointment. After a good start to the event in which they headed the Styles/May team, Mark and Leigh eventually finished 16th whilst Styles/May achieved a very good Sth place overall. Thus it seems, the UK's selection for. the (single) spot in the Tornado class for the 2004 Olympics is still very much an open question. 9K AK 6 KK Mark, together with his elder brother Paul, was a cadet member of MSC some 10-12 years ago, and they were contemporaries of Jenny and David Ball, Sam and Tom Ashley, Lucy and Damian Boreham amongst others. Mark and his brother sailed a 420 within the club and, I believe, Mark also crewed on one of the club's catamarans. 2K KK KK Like many another sailing club, the MSC can look back with some pride at the achievements of the multitude of individuals who have formed its membership over the last 50+ years. The club has always had members who have made their mark on the local Blackwater sailing scene and sometimes on the national and international scene as well. | From the earliest days we have had those members who have performed creditably on the cruising front as well as those who have done well on the racing circuit. | Malcolm Shaft's account of "Mona’s Travels” is merely the latest (albeit, perhaps the peak) in a long line of members who found satisfaction in cruising adventures. On the open racing circuit, MSC members have often rated in the top ten of their particular class, as well as producing the occasional national champion and even some who have earned themselves a world championship medal in bronze, silver or gold. However, as far as I know, the MSC has never had a member (or former member) who has made it to the sailing Olympics - but who knows, that might happen in 2004. For Mark's sake, let's hope so. Mike Boreham

St John’s Smith Square, London SW1 Saturday 13 September 2003, 7.30 pm For those London concert goers wishing to attend a conventional concert on Saturday 13 September, the James Allen Community Orchestra, under their conductor Rupert Bond, offers an unconventional programme at St John’s, Smith Square. The concert features the first London performance in many years of Alan Bush ’s lively and colourful Variations, Nocturne and Finale on an old English sea-song, Op.60 with pianist Mark Bebbington, and Elgar’s Sea Pictures with mezzo-soprano Rebecca de Pont Davies. The evening begins with Wagner’s Overture The Flying Dutchman, and also includes Mendelssohn’s Calm Sea and Prosperous Voyage and Benjamin Britten’s brilliantly evocative Four Sea Interludes from Peter Grimes. Malcolm Arnold’s ebullient Padstow Lifeboat brings the evening’s events to an end. Club Notes Commodore When the Executive, with the agreement of the members, formed Thirslet Sailing Club as a Company Limited by Guarantee, we were legally obliged to provide to Companies House two documents known as the "Memorandum of Association" and the "Articles of Association". The first defines in general terms the objectives of the Club and the second provides the general framework for the management and running of the Club. Of necessity these documents had to exist to allow the company to be registered to negotiate the purchase of the site and to allow members to transfer into it. The content of these documents is drawn in part from the "Marconi Sailing Section Rules and Constitution" and in part from the legal requirements of being a company. As with the "Marconi Sailing Section Rules and Constitution", these two documents can only be amended by a vote of the members in an Annual or Special General Meeting. There is then a third document which is the By Laws. In exactly the same way as in the "Marconi Sailing Section", these are issued by the Management Committee and the members can rescind any specific By Law(s) by a motion being put at an Annual or Special General Meeting. The Executive and Management Committees in writing the By Laws are taking the opportunity to restructure them into more defined sections, to better define the classes of membership taking account of views which have been expressed by a number of members and to revise the sub committees to better reflect the activity of the Club today. This is taking longer than the Executive visualised providing a problem as we approach the Annual General Meeting in that we will not be able to complete the exercise, but we need them in place to hold the AGM. The Management Committee has therefore concentrated on those sections essential to the AGM which are Section One, the membership classes - Section Two, Annual Subscriptions etc. - and Section Eight, The Executive, Management and Subcommittees. It should be noted that whilst we believe that we have identified the appropriate Sub Committees, we still have considerable work to do to define their Terms of Reference and therefore the exact composition of each one. We are publishing the complete By Laws in the form that we have currently agreed so that we can elect the Executive and Management Committees and conduct the other essential business at the AGM. You will also find the "Memorandum of Association" and the "Articles of Association" as deposited at Companies House in this issue. You will see that a great deal of hard work has already been done but understand that we need your support whilst the all-important fine tuning is undertaken. Having referred earlier to the Annual General Meeting, you will find the preliminary notice in this issue which includes the nomination form for the positions to be elected at the meeting. ECPR 2003 - ANOTHER FINE TEAM EFFORT Others will talk about the wind — or lack of it . Yet others will report tales of how they lost three places rounding Colne Point .... and regained them in the bar later. One of the great things about events like ECPR is that it gives everyone, no matter how small or remote their involvement, plenty to talk about. I will give thanks. Not just the thanks of the ‘ ..... and a list too numerous to mention’ variety but a more detailed celebration of all of those many people who contributed to another outstanding event on the international racing calendar. At a time of significant change within the Club I am given an opportunity to celebrate who we are and what we do — in an alphabetical listing of all that is ECPR: Considerations of readability lead me to the view that what follows will work best ifI ask my readers to accept now to my grateful thanks for anything at all they have done to assist the event. BAR operations is always something of a challenge for an event of this scale. Kevin Kirby pulled together a willing team of servers. Derek and Doreen Kirby and John and Mavis Weedon provided effective but benign management of another efficient operation. BRADWELL OUTDOOR CENTRE and TENDRING DC provide support craft and crews that add strength to our safety patrols in the Mersea and Jaywick sectors. CATERING has always been good at ECPR but we have long felt the need to provide a service that was more versatile and homely. Belinda and her excellent, smiling team achieved this ambition for us handsomely and the spontaneous applause for my remarks at the Awards Ceremony about them showed that our visitors appreciated the change too. _CHARLES ANDERSON may not have been seen or heard over the weekend but no one should doubt his involvement in setting up and breaking down — not to mention his usual demanding role in pulling together all the Safety cover. This year this included the creation of a formal Disaster Plan — a huge task. CLEANING was undertaken efficiently and quietly by Jan and her helpers. A marvellous job done under extreme pressure. ‘CLEAN UP- quick’ expresses our aims for the day after the event — the need is to remove all traces of ECPR activity and return the site to normal without delay. An almost invisible army of club members picked litter, cleared the bars, packed away the marks, removed signage and did all that was necessary to achieve that aim. COMMITTEE BOAT Duet, owned and crewed by Founder Member Mike Sissons, provided a decorative and comfortable base for the RO team. ECPR COMMITTEE is involved year —round in the preparation for and management of such a large event. Here is a flavour of what they undertake: e Clive Shenton — trophies, toilets and tape (red) Charles Anderson — safety (such a small word, such a large undertaking) Christina Hutt — Raffle, competitor safety equipment and committee victuals. Steve Cleaver — a brave and valuable late addition to cover safety matters. Nick Pavitt — ensures that PR matters are properly dealt with. Kate Williams — the Web site, the programme, the clothing, the gifts — superb! Kevin Kirby — essential liaison with the Cat fleet, volunteer rotas and more. FAST RESCUE fleet was once again strengthened by support from Steve Lamacq in Outspan and the Harlow Diver team. On Saturday we had welcome cover from the RIB Juggler and hope that we might see them at future events. FAST RESCUE RADIO NET was an important improvement to our safety arrangements this year. Roger Camp provided the expected calm and reassuring service. FIRST AID cover was provided by Fennella Thomas KEEPING VISITORS HAPPY seems to be a hallmark of the Club so far as those visitors who speak and write to me are concerned; many speak of ECPR as the friendliest event on the circuit. No surprises for us here — this is one reason whyI joined — but every club member on site can pat himself or herself on the back for contributing to the ambience. LAYING MARKS may seem to be a fairly unremarkable (sorry) activity until you realise that in order to position our inflatables at Colne Point and Weymarks Mike Richardson (wallet winner in the Raffle) and his team needed to give up a good part of a day of their own time. And we must not overlook the time devoted by Peter Tovey to the maintenance of the marks and ground tackle to ensure that the operation is glitch-free.

6 MARCONI RESCUE FLEET provided the professional service asked of them and thanks go to Barry Hutt, Ian Rawley, Tim Sweet, John Nisbit, Dennis Dear, Malcolm Stewart, Andy Masson, Roger Smith, Bob Shenton and David Ball. MARKING OUT the fields may seema bit of an indulgence if you view the rather haphazard layout that exists by late Saturday — but it is an important aid in directing people in the early stages of the build up and enables us to squeeze everyone in without the need to be too directive or officious. Our white line markers-out this year were Evan Davis and Christina (All White) Hutt. MARQUEE MAESTRO MIKE Waugh did us proud once again. MOTHER BOATS are the safety back bone of ECPR and can be one of the more uncomfortable locations from which to watch the Race unfold. Our thanks this year go to the following boats, their skippers and their gallant crews: Ocean Slipper (Frank Burgess); Juno (Jez Rowles); Swiftsure (Dave Steward); Shellseeker (Peter Culling); Pepper (Gordon Pewter); Rubicon (Roger Camp); Limbo Lady (Graham King); Boogie (Simon Elwell); Endeavour (Chris Hennah); Angel 2 (Peter Bloomfield); Green Panther (Mike Smith)and Killara 2 (Derek Gardner). NEIL, our Commodore, provides a welcome and reassuring presence throughout the weekend — giving a grunt here and a nod there to help ensure the smooth running of the event but providing valuable back up that can be called on in times of need. PRIVATE CHANNEL RADIOS were provided once again by Brentwood Communications and transported by Jenny Ball RACE OFFICER Mike Turner brings a wealth of experience to the role and had excellent support from assistants John Salmon and Graham Borgonon. Nick Miller and Anthony Monks gave valuable support as spotters during the finish sequence. RACE RECEPTION is a key area for an event like this. Competitors need to be dealt with efficiently and in a friendly manner; care needs to be taken to handle the finances correctly; handicap issues and a myriad other enquiries need to be dealt with and, last but not least, we need to sell Raffle Tickets and Clothing in support of the charity. Kate Williams led a team that included Alex Shenton , Marion X, Claire Davies, Sarah Davies, Jane Townsend and Dave Williams in the provision of a first-class service. RADIO OPERATOR John Pine comes back year after year and looks slimmer, fitter and more dapper every time. More importantly for us, he does a great job. RAFFLE management was provided by Christina Hutt and she was supported by Fennella Thomas and small army of other helpers. REFUELLING is important in a long distance series. Dave Bladon ensures that essential supplies are in place. RESULTS processing was again handled in the most efficient manner imaginable by Kate Williams and Jane Townsend. RNLI bring a stand, manned by Ron and Mary Greygoose that adds to the ambience. RUNNER- essential legs (and occasional eyes and ears too) for the OOD were provided by Sarah Davies on the big day and by Tim Dowley during the build up. SPECIAL SEASIDE SPOTTERS Tony and Jack Ferguson were deployed at Walton Pier at very short notice to deal with a potentially serious communications problem. They aided in the provision of essential information. That info led to the decision to shorten course and so they were able to go home again — without seeing a single catamaran! SPONSORS are not always easy to find but their contribution is essential. TERRITORIAL ARMY involvement was always under threat in 2003. In the event, the support given by Mark Mackenzie - Bell and his team was as good as we have come to expect and this despite the fact that the team were new to the event and using equipment that was completely foreign to them TRACKING TEAM TRIO Mike and Maggie Boreham and Barbara Davies have, for more years than any of them care to recount, provided an effective and efficient system of recording and reporting competitor positions along the course. Nice to have for reporting progress but absolutely essential in terms of safety. Quiet, too. TROPHY TECHNICIAN Mike Richardson gave his usual valuable support. TROT BOAT services and local support afloat were provided by Lucy Boreham, Joe Ashley, JamesTovey, Sarah Davies (yes, the same one — again), Claire Davies and Tim Dowley. TROLLEYS could be a nightmare but over the years an excellent system has been developed by Phil Davis. Thankfully, Phil did not see fit to protect his intellectual rights and so Steve Ash and his team adopted the system and took on the Trolley Parking and scrutineering role this year for the first time. They carried it out with great efficiency and good humour, making a major contribution to the smooth handling of a large number of craft to and from the water. WELCOME BBQ on Friday evening poses a challenge insofar as it is very difficult to predict the numbers on site. This year the numbers were high and so was demand. Barbara and Sarah Davies (do these people sleep?) had prepared a range of salads and served them with locally produced hamburgers and sausages. Their efforts paid off — for the first time in living memory this operation produced a profit and the customers, too, were well satisfied.

Chris Davies Cat Fleet By the time you read this the Piers Race will be a distant memory and for most of us sailing that day, that will not be a bad thing. The weather was glorious but the all important ingredient (wind) was at times fickle to say the least. But let’s not forget the reason for the race; to help children who are less fortunate than us. I would like to give thanks to many people, too many to mention, for their hard work and commitment. Our donation this year to the Cirdan Trust will be in the region of £9,000. Club racing has been very competitive this year, the chute systems on the F18’s seem to aid our speed going around the cans when working properly, even to the point that Steve Glynn (having had a few days at the F18 Worlds with son Mitchell) has added a 3TM sail to his Tornado. The latest news however is that Steve has now swapped his Tornado with son Mitchell’s F18 as he likes the kite so much! Congratulations to Steve and Mitchell who took the Nacra F18 to Belgium for the F18 World Championships; one of only 7 UK teams at the event, finishing a healthy mid-table in the silver fleet. Other fast cat events in the calendar this year included the F18 Nationals in Pwllheli, North Wales over the bank- holiday weekend. Two F18’s and 1 Spitfire attended from the club. Steve and Debbie Glynn, Christina Hutt and myself were the only “parents” in addition to the 10 young adults that came along with us, which at times felt like a 2TM! Cadet Week! COMPANIES ACT 1985 - 1989 COMPANY LIMITED BY GUARANTEE AND NOT HAVING A SHARE CAPITAL MEMORANDUM OF ASSOCIATION of THIRSLET SAILING CLUB LIMITED Name The name of the company is Thirslet Sailing Club Limited. Registered office The registered office of the company will be situated in England. Objects The company’s objects are: 3.1 to acquire and take over all or any part of the assets and liabilities of the present unincorporated body known as MASC, Beehive Lane, Chelmsford to promote sailing and to encourage social intercourse among the members of the company; 3.3 to establish, maintain and conduct a club for the accommodation of the members of the company and their friends, and generally to afford to them all the usual privileges, advantages and accommodation of a club; 3.4 to acquire by purchase, lease, or otherwise grounds at Marconi Sailing Club, Stansgate Road, Steeple, Essex and to lay out, and maintain the same for the sport of sailing and the benefit of its members and to build or otherwise provide a clubhouse and other usual facilities in connection with it, and to furnish, modify and maintain it, and to permit it to be used by members their friends and employees of the company and others, either gratuitously or for payment; 3.5 to acquire by purchase, lease or otherwise any other lands or property contiguous or near to the premises of the company, and such as may be deemed by the company likely to advance or benefit, either directly or indirectly, the interest of the company; 3.6 to manage, improve, cultivate and maintain all or any part of the lands and other property of the company, and to demise, sell or otherwise deal with and dispose of them, either together or in portions, for such consideration as the company may think fit, and, in particular, for shares, debentures or securities of any company purchasing them; 3.7 to purchase, hire, make or provide and maintain, and to sell or otherwise dispose of all kinds of equipment and other things required or which may be conveniently used in connection with the grounds, clubhouse and other premises of the company by persons frequenting them, whether members of the company or not; 3.8 to buy, prepare, make, supply sell and deal in all kinds of apparatus and equipment used in connection with sailing and in all kinds of liquors provisions and refreshments required or used by the members of the company or other persons using the grounds, clubhouse or premises of the company; 3.9 to hire and employ all classes of persons considered necessary for the purposes of the company and to pay them and other persons in retum for services tendered to the company salaries, wages, charges and pensions; 3.10 to promote and hold, either alone or jointly with any other association, club or persons, meetings, competitions or races associated with the sport of sailing or other athletic sports and to offer, give or contribute towards prizes medals and awards for the sport of sailing and to promote, give or support dinners, balls, concerts and other entertainments; 3:11 to establish, promote or assist in establishing or promoting, and to subscribe to, or become a member of, any other associations or clubs whose objects are similar or in part similar to the objects of the company, or the establishment or promotion of which may be beneficial to the company provided that no subscription may be paid to any such other association or club out of the funds of the company, except bona fide in furtherance of the objects of the company; 3:12 to support and subscribe to any charitable or public body and any institution, society or club that may be for the benefit of the company or its employees, or may be connected with the sport of sailing; to give pensions, gratuities, Christmas boxes or charitable aid to any person who may have served the company, or to the wife, widow, children or other relatives of any such person; to make payments towards insurance; and to form and contribute to provident and benefit funds for the benefit of any persons employed by the company; 3:13 to invest and deal with the money of the company not immediately required upon such securities and in such manner as may from time to time be determined; 3.14 to borrow or raise and give security for money by the issue of or upon bonds, debentures, debenture stock, bills of exchange, promissory notes or other obligations or securities of the company or by mortgage or charge upon all or any part of the property of the company; 3.15 to do such things as the directors consider to be in the best interests of this club and 3.16 to do all such other lawful things as are incidental or conducive to the attainment of the above objects or any of them 3.17 To retain within the Company all profits and surpluses to maintain or improve the Company's facilities. No profit or surplus will be distributed other than upon dissolution of the Company. Limited Liability The liability of the members is limited. Undertaking to contribute to assets Every member of the company undertakes to contribute such amount (not exceeding £1.00) to the company’s assets if it is wound up while he is a member or within one year after he ceases to be a member as may be required for payment of the company’s debts and liabilities contracted before he ceases to be a member and the costs, charges and expenses of winding up, and for the adjustment of the rights of contributories among themselves. WE the subscribers to this memorandum of association, wish to be formed into a company pursuant to this memorandum. COMPANIES ACT 1985 -1989 COMPANY LIMITED BY GUARANTEE AND NOT HAVING A SHARE CAPITAL ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION of THIRSLET SAILING CLUB LIMITED 1. Interpretation In these articles: 1.1 ‘the Act’ means the Companies Act 1985 including any statutory modification or re-enactment of it for the time being in force; 12 ‘the Club’ means Thirslet Sailing Club Limited; 1.3 ‘secretary’ means the company secretary of the club or any other person appointed to perform the duties of the secretary of the club, including a joint, assistant or deputy secretary; 1.4 unless the context otherwise requires, words or expressions contained in these articles bear the same meaning as in the Act but excluding any statutory modification not in force when these articles become binding on the club; 1.5 the masculine includes the feminine and, where appropriate, the singular the plural. 2. Objects The club is established for the purposes expressed in the memorandum of association. 3: Membership 3.1 The number of members with which the club proposes to be registered is 500 (Five Hundred) but the directors may, whenever the business of the club Tequires it, authorise an increase of members. : 3.2 Everyone that has an interest in sailing yachts, dinghies and similar vessels propelled by sails along with their families is qualified to be elected a member of the club. 3:3 The first members of the club are the signatories to the memorandum of association and these articles and every person who at the date of incorporation of the club had paid an entrance fee to, and was a member of, the unincorporated club known as MASC, Beehive Lane, Chelmsford, Sailing Section referred to in paragraph 3.1 of the memorandum of association, and who, on or before 31 December 2003, or during such extended period as the directors may determine, signs and delivers to the secretary of the club the form of membership prescribed by the directors. 4. Proposal of members 4.1 Except as provided in articles 3.3 and 8 every candidate for membership of the club must be proposed by one member of the club and seconded by another member of the club, to both of whom the candidate must be personally known, and who are to be responsible for his eligibility. 42 The application for membership of every candidate must be in writing, signed by the candidate and his proposer and seconder, and must be in the form that the directors from time to time prescribe. 5; Subscriptions $:1 The annual and other subscriptions and entrance fee (if any) payable by members of the club are to be such as the directors from time to time prescribe. 5.2 The directors may provide either generally or as respects any particular member or members for payment of annual subscriptions by instalments. 5:3 Every application for membership must be accompanied by a remittance to cover the entrance fee (if any) and the appropriate subscription from the date of application to the following 31 December and in the event of non-election the remittance must be retumed to the candidate. 6. Life members and Vice Presidents 6.1 On the recommendation of the directors any person being a member of the club may, at any general meeting of the club, be elected an honorary life member of the club without any special payment for such life membership. 6.2 A two-thirds’ majority of those present and entitled to vote is necessary for election of an honorary life member. 6.3 Every honorary life member is entitled to all the privileges and subject to all the duties of a member of the club during his life (subject, nevertheless, to the provisions of article 13) without any further payment of annual membership except in respect of Boat Permit, Winter Storage, and Mooring fees, and except in respect of his guarantee contained in clause 5 of the memorandum of association of this club. 6.4 The total number of honorary life members shall not however at any one time exceed the greater of five per cent of the total number of members nor twenty in number 6.5 On the recommendation of the directors any person being a member of the club may, at any general meeting of the club, be elected a vice president. 6.6 The total number of vice presidents shall not, however, at any one time, exceed ten in number. 7. Categories of Membership The categories of membership of the club shall be full member, family member, junior member, honorary life member, senior life member, honorary affiliated member, temporary member and student member and the rights attaching to each such category shall be subject to the express provisions of these articles and to the memorandum of association, and to any byelaws made by the directors of the club as provided below for the time being in force. 8. Temporary and other members The directors of the club may, upon such terms and subject to such regulations as they may from time to time deem advisable and subject to article 4, propose as members of the club: 8.1 persons who are visiting or temporarily resident in the district of Essex (‘temporary members’); 8.2 visitors; but there may not be more than 75 such members of the club at any one time. 9. Election of members 9.1 Every candidate for election (including candidates for election to the special classes of membership specified in article 8.1 and 8.2) must be balloted for by the directors of the club and a majority will exclude. 92 The name, address and description of every candidate, and the names of his proposer and seconder must be sent to the secretary in writing, and these particulars must be posted in a conspicuous place in the clubhouse of the club 14 days at least before the ballot 9.3 On the unanimous recommendation of the directors in meeting duly convened, the ballot may take place before the expiration of 14 days but not earlier than two days after the application of the candidate is received and not without the application being posted in the clubhouse. 10. Rights of members 10.1 Subject to the express provisions of these articles and to the memorandum of association, and to any byelaws made by the directors of the club as provided below for the time being in force, all members of the club are entitled at all times to use all the premises and property of the club in common, and to be supplied, at such charges as the directors from time to time determine, with whatever meals, refreshments and things are provided by the club for the use of its members. 10.2 Subject to the provisions of these articles every member is entitled to all the rights and subject to all the duties of a member of the club provided that temporary, junior and honorary affiliated members and visitors do not have the right to nominate or be elected as officers or directors of the club.

11. Notice of resignation Any member wishing to resign his membership of the club must give notice in writing of his intention to do so, addressed to the secretary and deposited at the 4 registered office of the club before 01 January in any year, failing which the member must pay the subscription for the next year. ° 12. Non-payment of subscriptions 7 12.1 Any member whose annual subscription is unpaid on 28 February in any year ceases to be a member of the club and forfeits all right in and claim upon the % am club and its property unless the directors suspend the operation of this provision, which they may do as regards any particular member on such terms as they determine at their discretion. 12.2 Where the directors have resolved in accordance with article 5 that the subscription of any particular member may be paid by instalments, this article applies to non-payment of any instalment, substituting the due date of the instalment for 28 February. 13. Expulsion of members 13.1 If the conduct of any member is in the opinion of the directors injurious to the character of the club or objectionable in any respect, that member may be required by the directors to resign, and, if he does not resign within one week, the member may (after he has been given the opportunity to justify or explain his conduct) be expelled by resolution of the directors and then ceases to be a member of the club, and all sums that have been paid by the member are forfeited. 13.2 A member expelled under this article may appeal by giving written notice of appeal to the secretary within 10 days from the posting of the notice of expulsion. b3:3. Upon receipt of a notice of appeal an extraordinary meeting must be convened within 14 days and, if that meeting passes an extraordinary resolution rescinding the expulsion, then the member must be reinstated as from the date of the resolution. 13.4 If any member is convicted on indictment of any criminal offence or is adjudged a bankrupt, or makes any composition or arrangement with his creditors or, being engaged in any profession, is prohibited by the disciplinary body of that profession from continuing to practice that member ipso facto ceases to be a member of the club but any person so ceasing to be a member may be readmitted to membership by the directors at their discretion. 13:5 Any member expelled in accordance with these articles, or otherwise ceasing to be a member of the club, forfeits all right to or claim upon the club or its property or funds or any return of fees paid and remains liable for any outstanding fees or charges due from him at the date of expulsion or cessation. 14. Rights of members personal The rights of a member as such are personal and are not transferable and cease upon his death. 15. Annual general meeting 15.1 The club must hold a general meeting in each year as its annual general meeting in addition to any other meetings in that year, and must specify the meeting as the annual general meeting in the notices calling it. 15.2 Not more than fourteen months may elapse between the date of one annual general meeting of the company and that of the next. 15.3 The annual general meeting must be held at such time and place as the directors appoint. 16. Extraordinary general meetings 16.1 All general meetings other than annual general meetings must be called extra-ordinary general meetings. 16.2 The directors may, whenever they think fit, and must, on a requisition made in writing by at least thirty members or members representing not less than one- tenth of the total voting rights of all the members having at the date of deposit of the requisition a right to vote at general meetings, whichever is the lesser, convene an extraordinary general meeting. 16.3 Any requisition made by the members must state the object of the meeting proposed to be called, and must be signed by the requisitionists and deposited at the registered office of the club. 16.4 On receipt of the requisition the directors must immediately proceed to convene an extraordinary general meeting. 16.5 If the directors do not proceed to call a meeting within 21 days from the date of deposit of the requisition, the requisitionists, or any of them representing more than one-half of the total voting rights of all of them, may convene such a meeting. 16.6 The expenses of notification of and the holding of a meeting called as a result of a requisition shall be borne by the requisitionists who shall deposit with the club a sum reasonably sufficient to meet the club’s expenses in relation thereto save that the club will refund to the requisitionists the amount of such expenses in the event that any proposed resolution made known by the requisition is carried. 17. Notice of meetings Accidental omission to give notice of any meeting to or non-receipt of such notice by any member does not invalidate the proceedings at that meeting. 18. Quorum 18.1 No business may be transacted at any meeting unless a quorum is present. 18.2 Save as otherwise provided in these articles, thirty members personally present is a quorum 18.3 If within half an hour from the time appointed for the meeting a quorum of members is not present, or, if during a meeting such a quorum ceases to be present: 18.3.1 if the meeting was convened on the requisition of members, it must be dissolved; 18.3.2 in any other case the meeting stands adjourned to the same day in the next week at the same time and place or to such time and place as the directors may determine and, if at the adjourned meeting a quorum of members is not present within half an hour of the time appointed for the meeting, the members present may form a quorum. 19. Chairman 19.1 The commodore, and failing him the vice-commodore, must preside as chairman at every general meeting of the club. 19.2 If there is no such chairman, or, if at any meeting he is not present within 15 minutes of the time of holding the meeting, the members present may elect one of their number who is a director to be chairman of the meeting. 19.3 If there is no director present, then the members may elect any one of their number to be chairman of the meeting. 20. Adjournment 20.1 The chairman may, with the consent of a meeting at which a quorum is present (and must if so directed by the meeting), adjourn the meeting from time to time and from place to place. 20.2 No business may be transacted at any adjourned meeting other than business which might properly have been transacted at the meeting had the adjournment not taken place. 21. Passing of resolutions 21) At any general meeting: 211 a declaration by the chairman that a resolution has been carried, or carried unanimously, or carried by a particular majority, or lost, or not carried by a particular majority, and 21:12 an entry to that effect in the book of proceedings of the club are conclusive evidence of the fact without proof of the number or proportion of the votes recorded in favour of or against the resolution, unless a poll is demanded by the chairman or by at least two members having the right to vote at the meeting or by a member or members representing not less than one- tenth of the total voting rights of all the members having the right to vote at the meeting. 21.2 If a poll is demanded in the above manner, it must be taken in such manner as the chairman directs, and the result of the poll is deemed to be the resolution of the meeting at which the poll was demanded. 22. Voting rights

22.1 Every member of the club may attend general meetings of the club but only full members, family members, student members, senior life members and honorary life members may vote at such meetings. + 22.2 22.3 No member may vote at any meeting unless all the money then due from him to the club has been paid. Every member of the club entitled to vote has one vote (save in the case of family members where there shall be one vote per family unit exercisable by one person over the age of 18) and no more, except that, in case of equality of votes, the chairman may have a second or casting vote. » 23. Proxy voting 23.1 On a poll votes may be given either personally or by proxy. 23.2 A proxy must be appointed in writing under the hand of the appointor. 23.3 The instrument appointing a proxy must be deposited at the registered office of the club not less than 48 hours before the time of holding the meeting at which the person named in such instrument proposes to vote. 23.4 Any instrument appointing a proxy must be in the following form: THIRSLET SAILING CLUB LIMITED [I or We], (name) of (address), being [a member or members] of the above named club, appoint (name) of (address), or, failing him, (name) of (address), as [my or our] proxy to vote in [my or our] name [s] and on [my or our] behalf at the [annual or extraordinary] general meeting of the club to be held on (date) and at any adjournment. Dated: (signature(s) of members(s)) 24. Directors 24.1 The directors of the club are the commodore, two vice-commodores, two rear-commodores, honorary treasurer elected as provided in these articles. 24.2 Four directors are a quorum at a directors’ meeting. 24.3 The commodore, and failing him a vice-commodore, must preside as chairman who in case of equality of votes may have a casting vote. 25. Officers 25:1 The officers of the club are the president, vice-president(s), commodore, two vice-commodores, two rear-commodores, honorary treasurer and secretary, all of whom must be members of the club. 25:2 The immediate past commodore is to be an ex officio officer of the club during the period of his immediate past captaincy. 25.3 The first officers of the club are :- President: Tony Benn Vice Presidents: Steve Glynn, Peter Clayton, Clive Shenton, Peter Bloomfield and Frank Bennett Commodore: Neil Pembleton Vice-Commodore: David Payne Rear-Commodore: John Salmon Hon. Treasurer: John Bird Secretary: Patrick Black 26. Remuneration No director or officer of the club, other than the secretary, may receive any remuneration for his services in the capacity of director or officer but nothing contained in these articles is to prohibit payment by the club of any sum to the secretary for clerical or other assistance. 27. Age limits There is not any age limit for directors and accordingly Section 293(2)-(6) of the Act does not apply to the Club. 28. Retirement of directors and officers 28.1 At every annual general meeting of the club, the officers and directors other than the secretary must retire from office. 28.2 The retiring officers and directors are eligible for re-election at the same or any other general meeting of the club. 29. Election of officers Subject as provided above, the election of officers other than the secretary and other directors of the club, must take place in the following manner: 29.1 Any two members of the club may nominate any other member to serve as an officer or director of the club, having previously received his assent. 29.2 The name of each member so nominated, together with the names of his proposer and seconder, must be sent in writing signed by all three of them to the secretary of the club at least 21 days before the annual general meeting. 29.3 A list of the candidates’ names in alphabetical order, with the proposers’ and seconders’ names, must be posted in a conspicuous place in the club-house of the club at least 14 days immediately preceding the annual general meeting. 29.4 Balloting lists must be prepared (if necessary) containing the names of the candidates only in alphabetical order. 29.5 Each member present at the annual general meeting and qualified to vote may vote for any number of candidates not exceeding the number of vacancies. 29.6 If insufficient candidates are nominated, the directors may elect a member or members to fill the remaining vacancy or vacancies. 29.7 If any candidate declines to serve after being elected, the candidate who has the next largest number of votes must be deemed to be elected. 29.8 If two or more candidates obtain an equal number of votes, the directors must select by lot from such candidates the candidate or candidates who is or are to be elected. 30. Appointment of secretary 30.1 The secretary of the club must be appointed by the directors for such term, at such remuneration and upon such conditions as they think fit. 30.2 The directors may terminate the secretary’s appointment and fill a vacancy in the office. 31. Casual vacancies 31.1 All casual vacancies arising amongst the directors or officers of the club must be filled by the directors. 312 Any director or any officer (other than the secretary) appointed to fill a casual vacancy must retire at the following annual general meeting. 32. Removal of directors The office of a director is vacated if: 32.1 his membership of the club is terminated in accordance with article 13.4; 32.2 he absents himself from meetings of the directors for a continuous period of six calendar months without special leave of absence from the other directors; or 32.3 he gives the directors one calendar month’s notice in writing that he resigns his office or 32.4 he is removed by extraordinary resolution passed at a general meeting of the club. 33. Accounts 33.1 The directors of the club must ensure that proper books of account are kept in respect of: 33.1.1 all sums of money received and expended by the club and the matters in respect of which the receipts and expenditure take place and 33.1:2 the assets and liabilities of the club. 33.2 The books of account must be kept at the registered office of the club, or at such other place or places as the directors think fit, and must always be open to the inspection of the directors. 33.3 The directors must from time to time determine whether, and to what extent, and at what times and places, and under what conditions and regulations, the accounts and books of the club, or any of them, are to be open to the inspection of members of the club who are not directors.

33.4 No member who is not a director has any right to inspect any account or book or document of the club except as conferred by statute or authorised by the directors. 34, Presentation of accounts 34.1 Once at least in every year the directors must lay before the club in general meeting an account of income and expenditure for the period since the preceding account. 34.2 A balance sheet must be made out in every year and laid before the club in general meeting, made up to a date not more than six months before such meeting. 34.3 A copy of the balance sheet must be sent to, or made available to, the persons entitled to receive notices of general meetings in the manner in which notices are to be given under these articles 21 days prior to the meeting. 34.4 Every account and balance sheet must be accompanied by a report of the directors and the account, report and balance sheet must be signed by two directors and countersigned by the secretary. 35. Powers of directors 35.1 The directors of the club may exercise all powers that may be exercised by the club and do anything that may be done by the club, except where under these articles or any statute for the time being in force the power must be exercised or the thing be done by the club in general meeting. 35.2 The directors may act notwithstanding vacancies. 35.3 The directors of the club may issue debentures, debenture stock, bonds, or obligations of the club at any time, in any form or manner, and for any amount, and may raise or borrow for the purpose of the club any sum or sums of money either upon mortgage or charge of all or any of the property of the club, whether present or future, or on bonds or debentures secured by trust deed or otherwise or not secured as they may think fit. 36. Byelaws 36.1 The directors of the club may from time to time make, alter and repeal any byelaws they consider necessary or expedient or convenient for the proper conduct and management of the club, and in particular, but not exclusively, they may by such byelaws: 36.1.1 regulate the terms and conditions upon which different categories of members and their guests, as well as visitors, may use the premises and property of the club; 36.1.2 fix the times of opening and closing clubhouse, and premises of the club or any part of them and the permitted hours for the supply of intoxicating liquor; 36.1.3 promulgate the rules to be observed and the prizes or stakes to be played for by members of the club playing any games on the premises of the club; 36.1.4 prohibit particular games on the premises of the club entirely or at any particular time or times; 36.1.5 regulate the conduct of members of the club in relation to one another and to the club’s staff; 36.1.6 set aside the whole or any part or parts of the club’s premises for gentlemen members, women members or any other class or classes of members, at any particular time or times, or for any particular purpose or purposes; 36.1.7 impose fines for breach of any byelaw or any article of association of the club and 36.1.8 regulate all matters that are commonly the subject of club rules. 36.2 The directors must adopt whatever means they consider sufficient to bring all byelaws, alterations and repeals to the notice of the members of the club. 36.3 All byelaws, so long as they are in force, are binding on all members of the club. 36.4 No byelaws may be inconsistent with, or affect or repeal anything contained in, the memorandum or articles of association of the club, or be in breach of any statutory provision. 36.5 Any byelaw may be set aside by a special resolution of a general meeting of the club. 37. Delegation 37:1 The directors of the club may delegate any of their powers to a committee or committees appointed by the directors. 37.2 With the exception of a sub-committee with less than four members or one concerned with the purchase for the club, or supply by the club, of intoxicating liquor, a sub-committee shall be chaired by an officer or director. 37.3 In the exercise of the powers delegated to it, a committee must conform to any regulations prescribed by the directors. 37.4 Any delegation of powers or appointment of a committee may be recalled or revoked by the directors at any time. 38. Audit An auditor or auditors must be appointed and his or their duties regulated in accordance with the Act. 39. Execution of Deeds 39.1 The club shall not have a common seal. 39.2 The club may execute any deed by the authority of a resolution of the directors and in the presence of: 39.2.1 at least two directors and 39.2.2 the secretary or another person appointed by the directors for the purpose. 39.3 The two directors and the secretary or the other person appointed must sign every instrument in the presence of each other. 40. Dissolution If the club is wound up, whether voluntarily or otherwise, the liquidator may, with the sanction of an extraordinary resolution of the club and any other sanction required by the Act: 40.1 divide among the members in specie or in kind, the whole or any part of the assets of the club and 40.2 vest the whole or any part of the assets of the club in trustees upon such trusts for the benefit of the members as he, with the same sanction, determines. 41. Notices 41.1 A notice may be given by the club to any member personally, by sending it by post in a prepaid envelope addressed to the member at his registered address or by posting it in a conspicuous place in the clubhouse of the club. 41.2 Where a notice is sent by post, service of the notice is deemed to be effected by properly addressing, prepaying and posting a letter containing the notice and is deemed to have been effected at the expiration of 48 hours after the envelope containing it was posted. 42. Headings The headings in these articles do not form part of them or in any manner affect the interpretation or construction of them. =*uoe Club Notes Commodore I can only apologise to members for the conditions at the Club as a result of the rewiring of the Cruiser Park.. When we decided to go ahead with the project after the delay caused by our acquiring the site, we were initially told that the contractor would dig the trenches, lay the cables and backfill the trenches in three weeks. As you are aware this has taken much longer but once started, we were rather stuck with finishing. Looking forward we have the Laying Up Supper on 8" November and the Annual General Meeting on 23" November. Immediately prior to the Annual General Meeting, we are holding the last AGM of the Marconi Sailing Section of the MASC. This meeting will receive the final account and vote on the dissolution of the section. One of the items to be resolved at the AGM is the name of the club for the future. I would like to thank Clive Shenton for organising the straw poll to establish the names that will be put to the vote. These are in alphabetical order: Marconi Sailing Club Stansgate Abbey Sailing Club Thirslet Sailing Club About the only downside that has come to our notice of buying the site from MASC, is that we are now being charged for the use of rooms at Beehive Lane. In order to keep the cost down we are holding the Executive meetings in our houses and the Management Committee meeting in the village hall at East Hanningfield. The other subcommittees are also making alternative arrangements. Partly for this reason and because of the reduced attendance last year, Roger Camp is holding the Cruiser Fleet AGM at the club and may not have any winter lectures. However I have received an invitation from the Royal Harwich Yacht Club and details of their lecture programme (printed elsewhere in this edition of Navigans). If you are interested in attending, contact their secretary direct: Colin Burrows Tel 01473 780319 or email secretary@rhy.demon.co.uk. In addition to the lecture, they can provide an excellent supper before the talk for £8.00 per head, again contact the secretary direct no later than the Monday before the talk. I look forward to seeing you all at the AGM on 23 November. Neil Pembleton Handicap Fleet End of season wash-up Here we are at the end of the season and it seems like months since I remembered to get an article to Matt in time for the deadline! Whilst I haven’t been afloat quite so much as I might have liked, the fleet has had a varied and interesting season, with a pleasing number of competitors in Sunday (and Wednesday night) racing throughout the season. I don’t mean by this to exclude our Saturday sailors, or those who like to creek crawl, cruise or just practise turning their boats upside down then the right way up again (my own favoured past-time) — racing is simply the more visible side of handicap fleet sailing at our club. It has been particularly pleasing to see new members joining and sailing regularly as part of the fleet, as well as the many new boats that have arrived and added to the variety of handicap boats. Dinghy Park One of the most obvious developments in the fleet during the season is certainly the change to the layout to the dinghy park. An obvious improvement, after early teething problems, was the increased widths of the gangways in the dinghy park, making rigging and de-rigging easier than in previous years. It also made use of the additional space afforded to us by the slight extension to the south of the park. I am aware, however, that as the season progressed, new members, and others bringing boats to the club later in the season, experienced difficulties in 2

a finding spaces for boats, and we had to resort to filling in gaps at the ends of rows. We will be looking at the layout again this winter to try and alleviate the problem for next year. If you have any comments or thoughts that may help us in this process, do contact me (details below) or Barry Hutt, Dinghy Park Secretary. Trailer Sailers Developing on the above theme, one area which I am keen to understand better is that of trailer sailers. These have, traditionally, been stored in the dinghy park during the summer, but the growing demand for spaces in the dinghy park has made this harder this year. It has been suggested that the best solution to this may be to dedicate an area in the catamaran park to trailer sailers - these spaces could be available both for summer and winter storage. Could members who consider their boat to be a day or trailer sailer (the definition is a little hazy within the club) please contact Roger Camp, Cruiser Fleet Captain on [redacted] or [redacted].co.uk. Roger will be able to advise you on a suitable location for your boat that will allow it sufficient space and car access for when you want to launch. Working Parties It is the working party time of year again. No date has yet been set for working parties, but, amongst other tasks, we need to complete one last bit of paving left over from last year. Please keep your eyes open for working party dates — ones in December and January are particularly good for burning off the excesses of the party season, and taking out your stress on a passing hedge. Handicap Fleet AGM — 6" December, 6 pm in the Clubhouse Before we get stuck into working parties, it’s time for another AGM. Since our normal Beehive Lane venue is now costing us, I propose that we hold our AGM at the club. As this is not convenient for everybody after work, I have set this for a Saturday, 6 December at 6 pm. My rationale is that the day gives fleet members the opportunity to be there, and the time gives us the opportunity to do our Christmas shopping first. I will open the bar both before and after the meeting, and following the lead of the cruiser fleet, we can get together a bulk order from the lovely Mayland chippy or the Chinese (it would be helpful if you could let me know in advance if you plan to attend and if you would be interested in the food — contact details below). I hope you will join us for what I hope will be a sociable occasion, where we can look at racing, cruising and capsize practise for all, and how we can improve it next season. I hope to see you at the Laying Up Supper (November 8" - last minute bookings may be accepted by Fenella) and at the club AGM on 23" November. Articles CADET WEEK 2003 During the preparations for “Cadet Week 2003” we started to look for an interesting logo for the T-shirts. Last year we had 50 years of sailing at Marconi Sailing Club so we thought it might be a significant anniversary for the Cadet fleet. We talked to several likely members in an attempt to establish a history of the early days but with not much luck until Maureen Ball, who spent a lot of time trawling through Navigans, came up with following; Birth of the Cadet Fleet in the Marconi Sailing Club - at Heybridge Before the days of the Cadet Fleet: In October 1957 a series of winter classes was proposed to teach the adult novices the theory of sailing. In the February/March 1961 Navigans there were proposals to consider creating a Junior Membership of the Club for youngsters aged 16-21. 1961 - The Cadet Fleet came into being at the Club's AGM on Thursday 30th November 1961 when 'R.F.S.' (Robbie Sims) reported on "the keen way in which the younger members of the Club have banded together to form a Cadet group and elected John Littlewood as their Cadet Captain designate. In the light of such enthusiasm the Club can do little else but make them an official branch of the sailing club." 1962 - Four Cadet Races were held during the 1962 sailing season; on 2nd June, 1st July, 2nd September, and the 4th race perhaps in early October (before publication of October Navigans). It was to be an irregular series of races for cadets aged under 18 who could sail either their own boats or boats borrowed from other members. In November 1962: The Payne Trophy (for Cadet Racing) was won by J. Bigden. The Fred Garrett Memorial Trophy was awarded to John Hutchings - presumably then as now, the trophy was awarded to the most outstanding cadet member of the year for reasons other than racing. 1963 - The Club began its move from Heybridge to Stansgate in the Spring of 1963. In the 1963 sailing season just two dates were mentioned for cadet races - 20th July and 21st September. In August a party of Marconi SC Cadets, with three Fleetwinds and a Graduate, were the guests of the Maylandsea Bay Yacht Club for their cadet week during August. Four days of handicap races and a variety of other events including a film show and a party for evening entertainment, followed by transport to Maldon for the Carnival Week fireworks. A party of cadets also visited the Blackwater SC for their cadet week and were guests at an evening party at the Blackwater Clubhouse. In November 1963: Payne Trophy won by Ian Shaw Fred Garrett Memorial Trophy awarded to Michael Eyre. 1964 - On 4th April a Cadet Party was held - ticket price 2/6d. Cadet Races were held on 18th April, 2nd May, 14th June, 20th June, 15th August, Cadet Open on 22-23 August. Cadets warmly thanked for all the help they gave at the Fleetwind Nationals with shore based help, manning rescue boats, providing refreshments and helping to clear up after the party. By July 1964: The small sailing boat "Brazil" had been given by Mrs Sutherland to the Club who planned to make it available particularly for the younger sailors. It was a glassfibre Solent Scow 11'3" long and rigged with a single terylene lugsail. It was much welcomed by the Club who had had to sell the Club's sailing boat 'Avril' late in 1963 because the cost in cash or volunteer time to restore her to useable condition was too great -'a casualty of the move to Stansgate.' Note that in July 1964 Navigans, just as today, members were being warned that venomous snakes may be infesting the sea wall and grassland area by the gun emplacement at Stansgate. Navigans stated that "should a bite occur, the nearest doctor holding snake bite serum is Dr Warren at Southminster, failing this, Chelmsford

6 hospital." Some grass clearance had been attempted but the grass is the responsibility of the River Board and as it was binding the banks of the sea wall it was grown there for a specific reason. In November 1964: Payne Trophy won by S. Darney Fred Garrett Memorial Trophy awarded to John Hutchings. There were now 46 Cadet members in the Club among the total of 513 subscription-paying members consisting of Marconi Employees/Family members; Associate (non-Marconi) Members/Family members, and Cadets. (Peter continues) This revealed that it was 42 years since the formation of the Cadet Fleet, not a traditional anniversary, but it identified John Littlewood as our first fleet captain. It also set us thinking that it would be nice to have a permanent record of past fleet captains. So what seemed to be a good idea would be to have a perpetual trophy for each new fleet captain to hold for the year. To this end we bought a shield and had it engraved with James Tovey as the first recipient. He then presented it to Sophie Hurrell-Smith. What we would like to do is to engrave a plate on the back with all previous fleet captains. So please own up! Contact me, Pete Clayton on [redacted] if you are a past fleet captain or know some one who was. John and Sue Littlewood kindly agreed to present the prizes at the end of Cadet Week this year. John made a short speech to open the prize giving, the notes from which I have included, with his permission, as they give an interesting insight into the beginnings of the Cadet Fleet. John’s notes When I was 13 my dad and I built a canoe in the dining room, much to my mother’s delight, which whilst half finished was kept in my bedroom. With school I went on an expedition to paddle from Maldon to Harwich. We reached as far as Clacton, sleeping over night at St Osyth on the beach. This was my first experience on the river. Two years later when I was 15 I joined the Marconi Sailing club at Heybridge with Roger Smith who now sails in the Solo fleet. The club was on a barge, the Mamgu, which had reached the end of her sailing career and was permanently moored. The Mamgu was rather a special barge, built as a yacht with a counter stern and lots of heavy wood panelling, bathrooms and a stone floored galley and needed a lot of maintenance. The club moorings dried out at low water and were spread around the Mamgu. Most weekends during the summer Roger and I would travel to Maldon on the train and walk down the canal to Heybridge. There were around 10 cadets who would arrive on a Friday evening or Saturday morning and stay until late afternoon on Sunday. We used to lark about a lot and spend most of the night shuffling around Heybridge basin after our half of cider in the Jolly Sailor until we could stay awake no longer. We would then sleep on the saloon floor. One night we had watched someone a little worse for wear try to drive his car into the canal, saved only by the mooring lines of a suitable positioned boat. For food we ate mostly chocolate, crisps from the galley, baked beans, bread brought from home and the rare delicacy introduced by one of our group, “Rice Pudding and Jam Sandwiches”.

We would crew for members in the racing, operate the rescue launch, borrow other members boats and hire the club boat — an old Gunter rigged half Decker called Avril. Like now, once a year most of the regular club members would sail to Osea for a day on the beach and the annual “Mud fight” just behind the shingle spit. Also, for several years we begged, borrowed or stole boats and sailed down the river for a weeks Dingy camping with a cover over the boom and wet sleeping bags. By what I have seen, we did not have the skills you have or the training you receive during cadet week. Most of my experience was gained crewing for Terry Hallam (you can see his name on the past Commodores board). He had an old Ramsgate smack converted with a Bermudan rig and a cabin. This had very leaky garboards that means we were very familiar with the bilge pump, especially when going to windward. We went to Mersea, Wivenhoe, Brightlingsea, Pin Mill, Burnham and the river Roach and I was very lucky to learn a lot about boats and the Essex coast. When I was 17 we started the move to Stansgate. This meant we had to get motorbikes but we were still able to camp at the weekends. We did have to change our Pub to the “Sun and Anchor”. These fields were empty and old Farmer Sparrow kept a bull where we park our cars today. It did have a fence but was still treated with a lot of respect. Where the concrete base stands we built the first club hut. This project was managed by an engineer called Alan Pratt. I can remember it being christened by Jack Bidgen, I believe “The house that Pratt built”. Alan was a fine engineer and mathematician. I later spent my first East Anglian Cruiser races, the Sunk race and Ostend race, amongst others, in a boat in which he was Navigator. We never got lost. I say this was the second building on site — the portaloo was the first. This was sited just to the west of the floodgates. If you were smart you would make sure you did not need to use it when it was full. You would find yourself carrying it to the river to empty first. WhenI started sailing, fibreglass and the Mirror dinghy were not invented. The boats we had were mostly plywood, Heron, Fleetwing, Enterprise, Osprey, Albacore, Flying Dutchman and a little later the Hornet and Fireball. We also used a number of older boats like the Blackwater one design and the International Sharpie, which are still sailed at Wells-Next-The-Sea in Norfolk. I hope you have enjoyed the week and will keep up sailing as long as I have. It has been a hobby which has held my interest all my life and which I have shared with my family, my friends and their friends. I think the best weeks in the year at the Club are camping and Cadet week. Long may it continue. Pete Clayton What’s in a name? With regard to your task of seeking members views of what our sailing club should be called. I would like to make the following comments. MARCONI SAILING CLUB Being a traditionalist I am in favour of retaining “MARCONI SAILING CLUB” for the following reasons;

1) The Club has recently celebrated its 50" anniversary and has a lot to be proud of, in particular the goof it has done for both “RYA Sailability” and “Cirdan Trust”. Regarding the former, “Marconi Challenger” can still be seen sailing at Grafham water plus of course there are other Marconi Challengers elsewhere giving pleasure to disabled sailors. 2) “MARCONI SAILING CLUB” is known throughout not only for its ability to host open events but also for the quality of its helms. 3) The Cruiser Fleet has taken the clubs burgee far and wide and can be seen in many clubs and ports of call where the name MARCONI is instantly recognised and respected. 4) Ifit were not for the dedication and foresight of our founder members, we would not have a sailing club at all. 5) As for the general public thinking you have to be a Marconi employee before being able to join. I would point out that over the past few years out non Marconi membership ratio has been far greater. It is up to us to make the public aware. 6) Let us not get carried away by the mismanagement of two so called financial directors, let us instead remember the technical achievements created under the name MARCONI and be proud of that association. 7) Lastly, I would point out Maldon District Council through the River Bailiff installed and charted a navigation mark off the clubhouse called “Marconi”. STANSGATE SAILING CLUB or STANSGATE ABBEY SAILING CLUB If we have to change the name then I favour either one of these titles. It states where we are, the name is at the top of the road leading down to the club and of course it recognises the connection with our President Tony Benn. THIRSLET SAILING CLUB I fail to see any connection with this name and our sailing club. Thirslet is a piece of land some two miles east of the club which shows itself only at low water and is an inconvenience to sailing although I suppose its fine for picnics. D. Kirby [redacted] News Ladder Safety A recent accident at club is a timely reminder to all cruiser owners to check the state of their favourite ladder. Often the ladder that is used for the boat is a cast off from home, it’s not safe to use for painting the house but it is safe for climbing on and off the boat in the cruiser park. The rungs of wooden ladders rot quickly when left in the open and it may not be obvious that they have reached their sell be date, until too late. An Aluminium ladder is a better alternative and even then it needs to be tied securely to the boat. In the recent incident, a ladder accident caused a head injury serious enough to warrant the air ambulance being called and landing on the hard to take the casualty to A&E. If only for the sake of the tenders that it cast adrift into the Blackwater, let’s try and make it the last time. 10 Racing 2003 Helm of the Year Series The Series this year took place on Saturday Sept 27, and was once again sailed in Bytes kindly loaned for the day by members. The Champions from 5 fleets took part, these being Roger Smith (Solo), Les Hurrell-Smith (Handicap), Jenny Ball (Medium Cat), Tim Wallace (Fast Cat), and Nick Miller (Cadet). The familiar format of 5 short races, where contestants sail a different boat in each race, was followed. Committee boat starts were used to provide a windward first leg of the course. Race 1 was set with a beat across the tide to No.1 mark, but unfortunately the force 2 wind faded just after the start, making progress against wind and tide tortuously slow. Nick made a very prudent long port tack up the tide from the start and this enabled him to establish a big lead at the windward mark, followed by Jenny, Tim, Les, and Roger. This remained the order at the end of the lap, but during the slow beat in lap 2 both Tim and Les managed to wriggle past Jenny to claim 2TM and 3TM spots. Jenny finished 4" in front of Roger. This race had taken significantly longer than the R.O. intended, due to the failing wind, and with no sign of freshening it was decided to take an early lunch. After lunch the wind had moved easterly but was not much stronger, so a different course was set in-shore in the bay near Ramsey Island. This provided protection from the tide and good viewing on the bank for the spectators. In Race 2 Nick again was quickest off the line and established a good lead at the windward mark from Jenny and Tim, with Roger and Les following at a respectful distance. Tim dived past Jenny on the first run to snatch a 2TM place that he held to the finish, with Nick again showing his rivals the way home. Race 3 saw Nick in charge once again, leading the others round the windward mark in the order, Jenny, Tim, Les, and Roger. The latter two were battling hard with Roger taking 4" on the second beat which he narrowly held to the finish. Nick was again in front early in Race 4, but Roger was clearly beginning to get the hang of the Byte as he led the others round the windward mark with Jenny in front of Tim and Les. The latter three were very closely matched on the reaches in what was the most competitive race yet, but Tim showed some good downwind speed to pass Jenny and Roger. Nick sailed serenely on to record another victory. Nick and Roger both sailed good first beats in the final race with Roger closing on Nick’s transom on the subsequent run in the only real challenge to Nick’s domination of the series. However, Nick soon opened a gap on the second lap and Tim and Jenny both closed up on Roger, passing him on the final beat. Nick received a warm round of applause as he crossed the finish line having deservedly claimed the title “Helm of the Year”. Results: 1° Nick 3pts; 2" Tim 8pts; ae Jenny 12pts; 4" Roger 15pts; 5" Les 18pts. Ladies Race Report (Saturday 16" August) Thirteen lady helms, some with crews entered the annual ladies series on a cloudy Saturday. Peter Tovey was the race officer. Race 1 Starting in an easterly 2-3, the fleet tacked close to the shore to keep out of the tide. First round the windward mark was Kate Williams in a GP14 followed by Michaela Glynn and Sopie Hurrell-Smith in Laser Radials with the rest of the fleet following closely behind. Halfway round the first lap the leading boats went round F mark the wrong way confusing some competitors. (Must have been the dodgy crew Kate had on board, no prizes for guessing who that was!). 10

i Fenella Thomas in the 420 got it right but was soon hauled by Michaela after re-rounding the mark with a downwind leg to M mark with the rest of the competitors in pursuit. Last years ladies champion Jenny Ball decided to go for a swim, leaving Michaela to finish first followed by Kate and Fenella in 3TM place. Race 2 An increasing wind, gusting up to F4 saw a reduced fleet of 10 boats come to the start line. Kate was again first to the windward mark followed by Michaela and Fenella. The reach over to X mark saw Michaela overhaul Kate while Sophie chased Fenella for 3“ place. In midfleet Jane Townsend (Miracle), Sophie Shaw (Pico), Anna Sacre (Laser Radial) and Jenny Ball changed places around the course with some competitors capsizing. Again it was Michaela first over the line, Kate took second place and Fenella just held off Sophie for third place, Jenny Ball was 4”. Race 3 Only 5 boats came to the start line for the final race. Michaela was first to round the windward mark with Kate and then Jenny in close pursuit. Sophie retired just after the start and due to the number of competitors Peter Tovey shortened the rave to one lap. Club Notes Commodore As you are aware this is the last time that I will be writing Commodores notes following my late decision to stand down this year for personal reasons. I am extremely pleased that Chris Davies has agreed to being nominated to succeed myself and wish him well in the post. The company formed to acquire the site requires that there are six "Directors" for legal reasons who form the Executive Committee. These are the Commodore, two Vice Commodores, two Rear Commodores and the Honorary Treasurer. Again you will be aware from the Annual General Meeting notice that Peter Clayton, Ray Ball, Clive Shenton, Claire Davies and John Bird will be filling these roles. I believe that this team, along with Pat Black as Company Secretary, offers a brilliant blend of experience, innovation and youth to lead the Club into the next phase of its development, independent of the MASC. The By Laws of the Club were published in last month's Navigans and included the new Sub Committee structure which we believe recognises the functions of the Club and new responsibilities placed on us as a company. I am pleased to see that people have come forward to fill the main positions on these Sub Committees and again that we have an excellent mix of experience and new talent. They, along with the Executive, form the Management Committee to take the Club forward into the future. Retaining the principles of the founder members whilst recognising the different requirements of today, both in relation to leisure time and legislation. This year has seen tremendous strides by the Club but I have been saddened by a number of incidents during the year; Traditionally the shingle strip between the hard and the scrubbing posts has been left clear by the dinghy fleets for use by tenders from the cruisers etc. On a number of occasions this year the area has been completely blocked during the lunch break by dinghies on trolleys. On at least one occasion this was largely caused by those returning first from racing not pulling their trolleys far enough up the hard to allow others to come onto it. On the last Saturday of the camping fortnight there had obviously been a party in the Dell Bar. On the Sunday morning it was left to Mike Smith and Chris Pitak to clean up the mess left in there. It would have been nice if some of those who had been involved on the Saturday night had done this. Again at some time during the same fortnight, a dinghy was dragged across the garden by the patio. Probably because of other boats blocking the way. Bob and Elsie Anderson were considerably upset by this after the hard work that they put in. The situation was not helped by a thoughtless comment made to them "What else do you expect, this is a sailing club". Yes, we are a sailing club but many unnamed individual members of the club put a lot of time and effort into providing the well equipped, smart and tidy club in which we all can take pride. Let's not destroy this aspect of the club through a few thoughtless actions. I feel privileged to have been able to serve the Club in the last two years but I could not have achieved the purchase of the site without the support of the other members of the Executive and Management Committee and most of all the whole hearted support of all of you, its members. I wish the Club and its members, all the best for the future. Neil Pembleton

Cat Fleet AGM The Medium Cat and Fast Cat fleet captains have decided to have a joint AGM this winter. The reason for this is twofold; active members of both fleets have reduced in numbers recently and most issues are common to both fleets. We are your representatives on the sailing sub-committee and we are there to relay your comments, ideas and complaints, but we can only do that if you let us have them! Contact by e-mail is best, but feel free to 'phone us if you want.
