Racing & Open Events Dart 15 Open Event (17/18 April) The first 2004 Dart 15 TT event was held at Marconi Sailing Club in Essex with a fleet of nineteen boats. We were particularly pleased to have 10 entries from Marconi itself which included some welcome newcomers to the racing fleet - we hope to see you on the water during the course of the season as well! The Saturday brought unusually mild and pleasant weather with a light breeze. The first race saw Bob Carter and Peter Richardson hard on the heels of George Carter who was sailing sprint mode. Bob kept close enough to George to take 1st place by only a few seconds on handicap, with Peter Richardson a close 3rd and Phillip Howden in 4th. The breeze had strengthened for the second race and brought some interesting gusts / lulls as it came offshore — particularly when the fleet sailed inshore to escape the strong Blackwater tide. George Carter, Bob Carter, Gordon Goldstone, Nick Dewhirst and Philip Howden led the fleet hotly pursued by Peter Richardson and Andy Chidwick. Unfortunately, Bob Carter was caught by one of the unexpected gusts and capsized, although he still managed to pull back to a respectable 8th place. The winds also caught out Bob Rowntree, Nick Pavitt and Patrick Ellum who also capsized during the course of the race. On Saturday evening - the club laid on a general knowledge quiz for our guest and club members which proved very popular. The quiz was one by a team of visitors - the "50 plus" team with a Marconi team "the Bar team" (Andrew Dowley, Eammon Browne, Tania Monks, Sophie and Clara Hurrell-Smith) coming second! Belinda Dowley and Glynis Monks provided an excellent evening meal and Andrew Dowley kindly ran the bar and provided music entertainment. Sunday morning brought entirely different weather conditions with force 6 — 8 winds. A reduced fleet of 9 boats set off on the traditional and popular figure of eight race around Osea and Northey Islands. Early starts meant four boats had to go back over the start line, but the fleet had pulled closer together again as it shot past the end of Osea Island in the strong breeze. The race was Closely fought all the way round with Tim Dieu de Bellefontaine finally taking 1st place, followed by Bob Carter, George Carter, Andy Chidwick and Nick Dewhirst. The strong winds held for the afternoon race - an exhilarating round the cans with an interesting downwind leg which claimed Eammon Browne as a pitchpole victim and a few close shaves for some of the other competitors! Andy Chidwick also capsized on the last lap which regrettably cost him 4th place. George Carter took 1st place followed by Tim Dieu de Bellefontaine, Nick Dewhirst, Bob Carter and Gordon Goldstone. The varied wind conditions made for some great sailing and some very interesting final results — but the clear overall winner of the event was George Carter. | would like to extend my thanks to the raft of people that helped make the event such a success which includes: Kate Williams, Dave Williams, Fenella Thomas, Tim Dowley, Andrew Dowley, Belinda and Kevin Dowley, Glynis Monks, Tim Wallace, Tina Hutt, Paul Metcalfe, Claire Davies, Sophie Hurrell-Smith, Kevin Kirby, John Nisbet, Jenny Miller, Nick Miller, Clara Hurrell- Smith, Andy Williams, Peter Ward, David Ball and Dave Russell. Results: 1st place - George Carter, Grafham 2nd place — Bob Carter, Grafham Water 3rd Place — Nick Dewhirst, Whitstable 4th place — Tim Dieu de Bellefontaine, Marconi 5th place — Gordon Goldstone Queen Mary, 6th place — Andy Chidwick, Marconi Other Marconi positions: Jenny Ball (7th), Eamonn Browne (8th), James Tovey (10th), Peter Richardson (11th), Richard Jones (14th), Dave Bladon (17th), Nick Pavitt/ Patrick Ellum (18th). George and Bob Carter show the home crowd Jenny Ball the way!! Dart 15 - "Catbert" [redacted].fsnet.co.uk

Topper Byte Open 18-04-2004 The first of the Byte open series was held at Milton Keynes S. C. on Sunday 18-04-04. The weather was good with a steady force 3 S/W wind. All Eight competitors from clubs around the country were keen to get racing on this tactically demanding lake. The weather at end of day consisted of wind and rain. Race‘: All boats crossed the start line after some hard challenging for the best position, which was the top end of the start line. Ray Smith won this first battle. Ray led the fleet around the course for the first 2 laps with the rest of the fleet hot on his heels, with many places changing on each leg. On the third and final lap the wind dropped to a force 1 and the fleet began to split. Ray began to drop back into the fleet. Nick Miller took up the lead until the last leg. Nick rounded the windward mark 50 metres in the lead and headed to the right of the lake and lost the wind. The rest of the fleet went left after rounding the mark. With very little wind every puff was vital. The fleet was slowly closing up on the leader. At the finish line Maggie Futcher was first, 2" Eddie Pope and 3° Nick Miller. There were only 2 boat lengths between 1*' and 3” place. A very close and thrilling race. Race2: Very little wind at the start, so very important to get a good start. Adrian Stell was the victor this time. Adrian led for the fist two legs of a three-leg race. At end of the first lap, 1*' Eddie Pope, 2nd Adrian Stell and 3" Maggie Futcher. The wind picked up during the second lap, at the end of which the wind had built to force 4. At the end of lap two the placing was ch Eddie, 2" Maggie and 3° Nick Miller. Maggie was caught out at the next mark by the wind and capsized. For the rest of the race places were changing throughout the fleet. Coming up to the finish line the first three places were being closely contested by Eddie, Adrian and Nick. Nick Miller was 1* over the line closely followed by Eddie 2"? and Adrian 3°, only 3 boat lengths between 1“' and 3%; a very challenging race. Race 3: At the start the wind had changed again to North, force 3. Adrian stell capsized on the start line, only recovering 8 seconds before the start. At the first mark, 1° Adrian Stell, 2° Nick Miller, 3° Ray Smith. End of the first lap, 1° Adrian, 2" Nick, 3° Ray, with the rest of the fleet in hot pursuit. On the third lap Ami Goodyear had cut through the fleet to take up 2" place. A very hard race at the front with 2” and 3” places changing nearly every leg. Nick had to finish no less than 2TM to win the open. Adrian had to win with Nick in 3° or lower. Crossing the line in qs place Adrian Stell, 2"? Nick Miller, 3° Ami Goodyear. The rest of the fleet was hot on the heels of the leaders. Very good and close racing by all competitors. Next open 01-05-2004 at Marconi S. C. The chairman is also vice-chairman of the Eastern region of the RYA so the meetings are a source of information on many matters beyond the Blackwater and Colne estuaries. The full minutes will be published at the end of April. Please contact me if you wish to see a copy. If there are any issues that you would like raised with BACSPA please let me know. RYA News e The EU proposal that the red ensign and other national European ensigns be defaced with the EU symbol has now been abandoned. e The RYA is trying to maintain the availability of red diesel beyond 2006. There is currently a EU proposal to restrict red diesel to commercial activities. e The RYAis trying to promote more voluntary work within the clubs and the RYA. Current feeling is that the RYA proposals may be well intentioned but are unrealistic. 10

11 e The way the RYA functions at the moment talented youngsters who do well in competitions are extracted from their clubs for national training under the auspices of the RYA. This robs clubs of the sort of talent that is needed to train the newer intake of dinghy sailors. | would imagine that sailing is not alone with this complaint. Local News e Construction of an array of wind generators on the Gunfleet sands has been postponed for one year. The RYA has submitted its objections to the phase 2 for wind generators in the Thames Estuary. e Further expansion of the container facilities at Felixstowe will take place over the next few years. The plans involve widening the main channel into Harwich Harbour. If small craft are to avoid the commercial channel they will be need to cross the shallow waters of the Harwich Shelf. e Redevelopment of the derelict site at the entrance to Brightlingsea Harbour will now take place in a revisedform. e Colchester Borough Council has published their development plans for the next ten years. These will be examined closely for any impact on the recreational use of the Colne. It is likely that Tendring District Council will also publish their 10 year plan. e Although TBT anti fouling has been banned for amateur craft for many years its use is now to be totally prohibited. However do not be tempted if you are offered a 45 gallon drum of the stuff at a knock down price. 12 View from the Rear i The sailing season is finally under way! It seems as though it has all cranked up very quickly — already we have had several points series events, in which the weather has gone from the sublime to the ridiculous, with a complete blow-out for races 1 and 2 resulting in instant cancellation, to the millpond conditions of the Easter Bank Holiday. At least the latter gave the cruiser fleet the chance to catch up with laying their moorings after some pretty awful weather. Already our first open meeting has been and gone. The Dart 15 Traveller event took place on 17" and 18" April, and saw 19 competitors in the event. It was particularly pleasing to see the high turnout from Marconi’s own Dart 15 sailors. Saturday saw the best of the weather, but with the winds increasing during the day. Sunday morning dawned with very high winds, and some competitors thought better of it and went home. Ten boats competed in strong and challenging winds, but George Carter from Grafham held his own to win the series. We have several other open meetings on the horizon. The Byte fleet join us on Saturday 1 May, and the Osprey fleet on the 2” and 3” May. Both these fleets are new first-time visitors to the Club, and | am sure that everyone will welcome them. Both should make for good spectator sport, too, although | hope we don’t distract the attention of our members during our own Bank Holiday racing on the Sunday and Monday! Please do come and support these events. Don’t forget too that the Solo fleet arrive for their annual Marconi Open on 15" May. = And the fun doesn’t stop there. As you will see elsewhere, we have given the Marconi Challenge Cup a new ‘look’, transforming it from_a Saturday open with low attendance to a day-long pursuit racing event for all of you who love to pursuit race but can’t always get to the club on time for Wednesday evening racing. It should a great event, with something a bit different for Sunday 6" June. Visitors to the Dinghy Show at Alexandra Palace may have encountered the ‘Top Club’ stand. ‘Top Club’ is an independent event, in which clubs will enter a team of three boats, one slow, one medium and one fast (all monohulls, I’m afraid). The organisers are allowing 80 clubs to enter the event in September, to be held at Grafham Water. Marconi has a team place reserved, and we propose using the late May Bank Holiday racing to select a team. Anybody who is particularly interested in being part of the team should contact me. Further information is available at www.topclub.org.uk. Thereis not much to report yet on the cruiser sailing or racing fronts, unless anyone was competing to be fi rstiin the water, or fastest application of antifoul. The handicap fleet though has announced two dates for handicap fleet cruises. The first is on 19"" June — see the noticeboard or speak to Dave Ball for more information. Last but not least, Mike Taylor has recently successfully completed the RYA Club Racing Coach course. This is the first step on the path towards one of our ‘Foresail’ ambitions, toimprove training for the over-18’s at Marconi. Mike will be offering race training to monohull sailors on Saturday 22TM May. Anybody interested should contact Mike directly (details elsewherein this Navigans). Format will depend upon whois interested and what their needs are. At this time, we can’t offer the service to the catamaran fleet — if any cat sailor would like to volunteer to do the course so that we can expand the training programme, please get in touch. See you on the water — | hope there is enough going on to interest everybody! Open Day 5th June 2004 Open day is our opportunity to show off the club that we have worked so hard to preserve. It is an ‘ALL-HANDS-ON-DECK’ event for us to attract new members and re- assert our presence locally. For it to be successful, we will need as many members as possible to play an active part in the day. There are several areas in particular in which we are looking for volunteers: Vessels and Helms We want our visitors to be able to get on the water. To make this happen we need dinghies, catamarans, windsurfers and cruisers of all shapes and sizes available and with helms. Old Kit Most sailors | know have sheds/ garages/ lofts full of old lifejackets and waterproofs. It is important that we provide buoyancy aids as a minimum to our visitors, and all loans will be appreciated. Support Boat crew We have a few names for support boat helms/ crew, but if you feel that your expertise would be best used here, please get in touch. Site Preparation If we want to show off our club, it needs to be looking it’s best. We have made a solid start to this with the ‘homepride’ initiative, fixing the road/ windsurfer lake, and starting to improve the hard. Before 5* June, there will be many tasks to undertake to make sure we have the place spick and span. Please volunteer if you can help tn this area. Ground Crew During the day, we will need meeter-greeters, activity coordinato;s, bar people, reception, trolley dollies, glass collectors, bouncy castle minders, to name but a few. Tell us where you can help. Tour Guides When our visitors arrive, many, if not all, will need to be shown around the site, and talked through the activities of interest to them. The more varied our group of ‘tour guides’, the better! If you are into sales, we would love your help in this. Everyone can bring a friend or colleague who is interested in sailing. If they don’t join themselves the might tell someone else about us. Advertising posters are available - tell us how many you would like! The day will start at 1000 BST for a briefing for our own happy gang, and we will invite visitors to join us from 1100 BST. Club Notes Commodore’s Comments | write this at the end of the first decent weekend for some time. After a pleasant couple of days on our own boat it was great to come back to the Club and see so much activity going on. The Solo Open was the main attraction on the water and the car park (drying out well now) was nicely full both of vehicles of those involved in that event or others doing their own thing. There was enough wind to make things enjoyable and a good time was had by all. Our visitors once again reported favourably on a friendly and warm reception — so well done to everyone who put in effort to make the weekend a success. Speaking of successes — Open Day on June 5" deserves to be a success since a lot has gone into the planning. Of the three main ingredients for a good outcome, two are difficult to predict or control: the weather and the number of visitors who turn up. The third aspect is your involvement and that is easier to influence — if you are willing to be influenced. Please do turn up to support the event and do please bring a friend or acquaintance to see what we offer. East Coast Piers Race, as most of you know, is an event close to my heart and | know that many of you share my enthusiasm for the support we are able to give to Cirdan Sailing Trust. | was fortunate to be invited to join them for their Patron’s Day aboard Xylonite and Duet sailing on the Orwell and to accept on your behalf their thanks for all we do for them. Somewhat unexpectedly, the highlight of the day for me was to get to talk at length to some of the crews who tutor the disadvantaged and often troubled young charges who are their guests in a normal working week. Hearing the sort of issues that they are involved with and their stories of the impact they can make in difficult circumstances was a rewarding experience. A couple of recent occurrences lead me to make just a couple of comments about personal safety. At this time of year more than perhaps any other there is a lot to be done, a temptation to take short cuts and sufficient time has passed since last season for us to have forgotten some of the safety lessons we suffered previously. So a simple plea — please be careful around your boats and around the site; use the proper equipment (if you don’t have it you can be fairly sure that the Club or another member has) and don’t take chances. We all do it from time to time and luckily for the most part we get away with it — but often our mistakes are cause by oversight rather than foolhardiness. So, might | make so bold as to suggest that where any of us sees someone apparently needing help or advice we tactfully give it — rather than suffering regrets later. After all, self-help is what we are about; it is probably better that we give that help sooner rather than later. | look forward to more weekends of the sort we have just enjoyed and to seeing you and your families on the water. Chris Davies Vice Commodore Grasscrete Working Party | believe the Grasscrete Project has already made a big improvement to the Environment at the Club. However it needs a bit of fine tuning to get it really right. The holes in the concrete are already growing grass and eventually | expect the area will look like a lawn, but a lawn which we can park on in the winter and run tractors and heavy trailers over. The topsoil in the holes has sunk down and needs to be topped up. | did about 10% of the area in 3 hours, so a gang of ten working for 3 hours should be able to do the whole area. Please bring spades and hoes if you have them. A pair of stout boots is also very useful for firming in the new topsoil. | will arrange for topsoil and grass seed etc. The Working Party will be on Saturday 29th May starting at 11.00 am. I hope you can join me. Clive Shenton [redacted].co.uk [redacted] [redacted] Solo Open Event The sun shone, the wind blew — what better recipe for a successful Solo Open meeting at Marconi S. C. on the River Blackwater in Essex on 16" May? 22 boats including 13 visitors enjoyed the sunshine and estuary sailing at its finest in the fourth meeting of the Solo Eastern Travellers series sponsored by Rooster Sailing. The preceding day had been taken up with a training session from Solo Class stalwart and boat builder Tony Thresher resulting in some aching limbs come the Sunday reveille! In a light Easterly the first race started on the flood tide and getting a good start and minimizing the effects of the tide was paramount. Jerry Garner led at the first mark and Godfrey Clark got away to a good start only to misjudge the tide at the windward mark and let three other boats through in the process. Jerry Garner led at the leeward mark and consequently led through to the finish, followed by Steve Ede and Godfrey Clark. The tide had just turned by the start of the second race calling for different tactics to be deployed. Nevertheless Jerry Garner got a useful lead again with Godfrey Clark again in the chase. Godfrey very nearly triumphed by better judging the angle of the finish line but Garner got the verdict of the “photo-finish” to give 2

3 him an unassailable winner’s position in the event. Steve Ede came third. Race 3 started with the wind strengthened by the sea breeze now a force 3. This time Steve Ede led all the way round pursued by Garner and Clark with regular visitor David Walford claiming the 4" spot and local boat Michael Taylor coming in 5". Jerry Garner has changed his home club to Papercourt which has clearly honed his tidal sailing ability to win at Marconi after several years of visiting. Race Officer John Weedon set some interesting courses and at the prize giving Commodore Chris Davies welcomed the visitors and thanked them for their support as well as thanking all the Marconi Club people who had made the day a success. Jerry Garner also thanked the club for putting on a good meeting, especially the Race Officer, rescue crews, the help with the launching trolleys and the galley. Thanks are specially due to Frank Burgess and son Mark for use of Ocean Slipper as the committee boat once again. Marconi Sailing Club also claimed the 8"" spot John Salmon and 11" Ron Greygoose, 12" John Burgoyne, 13" David Ball in a borrowed boat, 14" Martin Hall, 15" Claire Davies, Rear Commodore also in a borrowed boat, 16" John Strange and fleet captain John Nisbet in a strange lapse of current form at 18”. Roger Camp, Cruiser Fleet Captain Tel: [redacted] or email: [redacted].co.uk Sailing Secretary As | write this we have only one race to go in the Spring Points Series, the presentation for this series will be at the club on Sunday 20th June. A reminder about the Marconi Challenge Cup, this will take place on Sunday 6th June. The day will consist of two "pursuit" races with a similar structure to the club's Wednesday evening race. As opposed to the normal start sequence all boats start from the hard. Handicaps are calculated prior to the start with a relevant amount of time deducted, the slower vessels leave first with the faster boats going later. Many Thanks and Safe Sailing Les Hurrell-Smith Telephone [redacted] [redacted].com Cruiser Moorings There has been some recent concern expressed by club members about unoccupied Cruiser moorings that sink just below the surface at high tide springs. In response | reproduce below Peter Claytons comments which | hope will go some way to explain the problems we have and what we can do to sort out the few moorings where this problem occurs in the first weeks of the sailing year before the cruisers are launched. “The moorings at Stansgate are laid on a matrix determined by minimum chain lengths for the mooring to be secure, this then fixes the centre distance and the between row distance to ensure that the moored boats do not come into contact with each other. All the deep water moorings which are now laid were checked for correct chain lengths and condition this year immediately prior to laying. The problem of sinking buoys could be solved by longer chain but as ever its not as simple as that. Increasing the chain length also increases the swinging circle and thus the danger of adjacent boats hitting each other. You could increase the buoy size to overcome the problem but this has its own problems due to the relatively exposed conditions at Stansgate. Too large a buoy for the size of boat means that in rough conditions the spring effect is taken out of the mooring and very high snatch loads can occur between the buoy and the moored vessel which can and has caused the vessel to break-away. The actual problem at this time of year is exacerbated by high spring tides and the fact that a lot of the moorings have had no boat on them. Once the mooring has been used the slack in the ground chain is pulled to the middle allowing the buoy to float. Later in the year and even now an accumulation of weed or debris round the mooring can cause it to be pulled under. It can be a problem identifying the moorings which are giving problems. We leave the mooring barge in the water usually until Whitsun to address this and any other problems we may have with moorings. It is a problem we are aware of, take seriously and attempt to solve. If moorings can be identified with a specific problem let me know and we will fix it.” Editor

Editor A reminder of the club procedure for the supply of mooring chain The stock of chain kept at the club is ordered in January. The amount that is purchased is based on the following; requests from members, the number of new members and a little extra for emergencies. The stock of chain is not inexhaustible. During February, March and April this year the vast majority of mooring owners checked their moorings and came to me for chain, shackles and anodes, | was able to help these people. Some people did not examine their mooring until the day before laying and then asked for 100ft of chain, not unsurprisingly it was not available. It is essential that members check their moorings in good time and notify me early in the season if they require large quantities of chain. If that rule is followed | will be able to help them, by May it is too late. All chain and shackles need to be paid for before leaving the garage, the job of the chain bosun is to help members with the otherwise difficult task of getting quantities of chain on to site. The garage is not a general chandlers, we don’t hold accounts for anyone. This year | broke this rule twice, | am still waiting to be paid by one forgetful member who owes money from Good Friday. | hope this gentle reminder will jog his memory. Don Holdsworth Chain Bosun

View from the Rear Some very pleasant weather has made for good sailing over the last few weeks, with a host of open meetings making the most of it. The visiting Bytes on 1*' May had glorious sunshine, but not a lot of wind. After the first race had to abandoned due to the tide being rather stronger than the wind, more success was had with short, inshore courses in the afternoon. Pleasingly for the home club, the event was won by our very own Nick Miller. A fleet-let of Ospreys joined us for the remainder of the Bank Holiday Weekend, with event centred around pathfinder starts. From the sublime to the ridiculous, this group were caught in a squall on the Monday, along with some of the club racers, but all came home safely. The event was won by the Class Chairman and local sailor, Will Odling. Both the Byte and Osprey fleets were visiting us for the first time. Now that they have had the ‘Marconi Experience’ we lock forward to welcoming them back in even greater numbers in the future. A more established open was held over the weekend of 15" and 16" May. During the training day, Solo sailors discovered that they were quite capable of tying themselves in knots if they thought too much about their tacks and gybes! | am delighted to report the first outing of the replacement club Solo was a success — the sailor in it was a new member who has yet to acquire a boat, and, just as pleasing, it didn’t sink. The open event on the Sunday attracted 22 boats, most of them visitors, confirming the event's popularity. Steadily increasing winds made for some great competition, and an enjoyable time was had by all. Many thanks to all Fenella Thomas, Mick Taylor and John Nisbet and his Solo fleet ‘gang’ for all their hard work in organising these events. Our own club racing has seen good turnouts lately, with a pleasing increase in the cat fleets in particular. BJRC races have started, and the first Marconi cruiser race takes place over the Bank Holiday weekend, with a race around to Burnham. In chronological order, here’s what else we’ve got coming up this month.... e Wednesday Night Pursuit Racing starts, 2"° June — Tell the boss you have to leave work early, and enjoy a mid week race; e Open Day, 5" June — All hands on deck, please, for this opportunity to promote the club and recruit new members. Speak to your fleet captain to find out how you can contribute; e New Members Evening and Members Barbecue, 5"" June — relax after the Open Day over a burger and a pint of Fosters; Marconi Challenge Cup, 6" June —A day of pursuit racing for all; e Summer Points start! 13‘ June - If Spring Points are too chilly for you, see how many points you can get in the Summer Series; e Spring Points Prizegiving, 20" June - If you competed in the Spring Points, you'll be keen to be here after racing on the 20° to collect your trophies! Club Notes Commodore’s Comments Open Day was notable for a number of reasons: support from members was superb; against the odds, we managed to make the site presentable and the weather was fantastic. Our publicity strategy worked and the overall result was that over a hundred families turned up and signed in on the day. (One or two more turned up on the following day — and the publicity will bring in still others as the weeks go by). As | write this almost 20 have signed up for membership and quite a few more are expected to return forms shortly. So, a success by almost any standard — as an example of members’ collaboration; as an enjoyable social event; as a general publicity vehicle and as a recruitment device. Congratulations to all of you who contributed in any way. There was one member who misconstrued my earlier requests for high levels of help — he appeared, right in the middle of our busiest time, on the roof of the clubhouse. Oh, well..... The new members will surely take advantage of a number of planned events that are sure to show the Club at its very best. The first that comes to mind is Fun Day when all members from all fleets can come together for some light-hearted activity and serious socialising. In a rather more serious and intense vein we can look forward to the 17""” running of East Coast Piers Race. If you are not a competitor there is a lot you can do to contribute to the smooth running of this large, complex event. | would urge Cruiser owners to contact Charles Anderson now with offers of Mother Boat support. | know that Charles or Clive Shenton will also be pleased to receive any other offers of support from members to help with a wide variety of tasks, many of which can be broken down into short time slots. You don’t need to commit for the whole weekend and any help you can give will be greatly appreciated. All our efforts will, once again, be focussed on the important support Marconi SC provides through ECPR to Cirdan Sailing Trust. We are slowly catching up on issues affecting the appearance of the site after a long period of disruption and change. Routine maintenance of grass on lawns and parks, strimming the margins, dealing with growth on the sea wall and sweeping the hard are carried out by a large team of members operating on a rota basis and we should be grateful to all of them for all they do. Nevertheless, there are times when gaps appear in the rota. Nature does not recognise such disruptions and growth continues apace — leaving us with a bigger job when the work does get done. The work is actually quite rewarding and usually machine — assisted — so if you feel able to get involved please do volunteer (by speaking to Dave Steward in the first instance). Looking after your own patch and the surrounding area is important too — as is the correct disposal of rubbish. Please do your bit to keep the site presentable. A beacon in all of the above is the maintenance of the garden area of the Commodore’s Lawn by Elsie and Bob Anderson. Their week-in, week-out attention to this task provides pleasure for us all. There is sad news this month about the untimely deaths of one member and one ex-member — lan Airies and Brenda Robinson. | have written on behalf of the Club to Angela Airies and to George Robinson to offer our condolences to them and their families. Chris Davies Vice Commodore Progress on the groundworks Thanks to Clive (and others) the grasscreted area is beginning to look good and will improve as time goes on. Thanks Clive for all the (considerable) time that has been dedicated to this task. Please remember that vehicles and tractors are not to use the grasscreted entrance to the cat field. It is hope eventually to get some grass growing on the bare areas adjacent the grasscrete and this won’t happen if subjected to vehicles. Skips - where we put them The “Wasteater” skip has been moved so as to be less of an eyesore. As | write it is parked behind the hedge near the race cabin. This is still far from ideal and the matter is under discussion. Who knows, it might have moved again by the time you that read this! We are also actively considering alternative methods of disposing of domestic waste on the site. Skips — what you put in them Please note that our contract with the waste company is for the collection and removal of domestic type waste only. This is mostly from the rubbish bins in the clubhouse but can also be from boats or campers. Occasionally optimists will place bulky items near the skip in the hope that the driver will take them. He won't. The Wasteater lorry compacts the waste so he is unable to collect scrap metal, old furniture, etc. Clubhouse cleaners Unfortunately June and John Rogers were unable to continue to clean the clubhouse. They were good enough to stay on until the beginning of June to ensure that the clubhouse was presentable for Open Day. | am pleased to announce that Julia Whyte has agreed to take on the work and by the time you read this some of you may have met her. Please make Julia welcome at the club. Please also make Julia’s job as easy as possible by considerate use of the club.

Clubhouse cleaning, your help please Elsewhere in this edition of Navigans you will see an impassioned plea from Maureen about the state of the clubhouse and the problems involved in keeping it clean. Clive Shenton ECPR Chairman Sailing Secretary Report Well at last we seem to of been blessed with hot weather, we can all put those dry suits away and start using our "shorties." All the results for the spring points series are now published, the winners are as follows. In the Solo Class John Salmon; Handicap, Dave and Kate William's, Medium Cat, Jenny Ball; Fast Cat Tim Wallace and in the cadet series Anthony Monks. Well done! The prize giving will be at the club after racing on Sunday 20th June. There are still several races left in the Bank Holiday Series, following the last race John Nisbett has moved to the top of the table in his Solo. Don't forget the summer points will be published as an am/pm series. The weekend of the 5th and 6th of June proved to be a very busy with both the open day and the Challenge Cup. The challenge Cup was a very different format this year, 32 entrants, | hope all enjoyed the unusual format of the two pursuit races. This was to the best of my knowledge a first so any feedback would be appreciated. Well done to Brian Spencer for the demanding role of organizing this event, congratulations must also go to Rory Ash for spending so long afloat and managing to hold off much faster vessels for so long. | certainly found it an entertaining day which proved that the difference between cats and monohulls is more than the number of hulls! Well done to Tim Wallace for such a resounding win. Dave Hewes Cruiser Fleet We have had a busy month starting with the shakedown cruise to Burnham with 21 boats going round and 50 people sitting down for a meal at the Swallowtail. We had a good sailing wind for the race on the Saturday and a pleasant sail back into the Blackwater on the Monday. Some of us touched bottom on occasion but one, who shall be nameless, missed the Crouch completely and only realised that he was off course when he spotted a container ship. The Club open day exceeded all expectations with, | believe, over 300 visitors. It certainly seemed like it on the hard throughout the day. | would like to thank Simon and Suzanne Elwell, John Walker, Frank Burgess, Nick Hillman and Hillary and Derek Gardiner for taking visitors out for a sail throughout the day, not to mention those that | press ganged on the day for crew. Ata rough guess | would think that around 70 visitors went out on cruisers during the day. As | write this, we have just returned from the watercress run with 15 boats locking into Heybridge and 45 people for the evening barbeque. Fortunately the rain held off until we were about to enter the lock on the return journey when the heavens opened. Why is it that an outboard will run for over an hour on a tideless river but gives up the next day when you have to row against the tide from your mooring? Moving on to forthcoming cruises, we have a trip to Brightlingsea on the weekend of the 3% and 4" July and a week’s cruise to Ramsgate, Dover and Chatham on the week commencing 31*' July. Lists will be appearing on the noticeboard shortly. The ECPR is on 24"/25" July and the Club is in need of more cruisers to supply safety cover. If you can help, please contact either Charles Anderson or myself or put your name on the list on the Club noticeboard. Long stay car parking for those off cruising is to the east of the waste oil tank, please don’t park in the cat or dinghy fields as these are used for camping pitches on the ECPR weekend and camping fortnight. We still seem to have a pile of unclaimed tenders. These are by the waste oil tank and if they are not claimed within the next six weeks they will be disposed of. Some of these tenders have been kicking about the site unused for about three years to my knowledge. There is also a large tender by the name of “Polly” which appeared in the tender rack recently and was taking up three spaces. If the owner would like to contact me we can sort out somewhere to store it. As a reminder, your mooring number is your rack space number i.e. if your mooring is C10 then your rack space is C10. Roger Camp, Cruiser Fleet Captain Tel: [redacted] or email: [redacted].co.uk

News Brenda Robinson Very sadly, Brenda Robinson died on the 2" June 2004. George and Brenda Robinson were Marconi SC members for many years and are probably best known for their boat called "Freya" They left the Marconi club in 1996 and moved to the comfort of a marina berth in Tollesbury before going out to Australia for five years. Brenda contracted cancer whilst out there and successfully recovered from it. Only two months ago she was diagnosed to have secondary cancer and was bravely undergoing treatment for it. She appeared to be making fair progress with her fight against the cancer but unfortunately she lost her battle and unexpectedly but peacefully passed away. Brenda will be remembered for always having a cheerful and carefree disposition and will be greatly missed by George and her two sons Andrew and David. Greetings to you al: Chris Davies Commodore Club Cleaning Having tried it, | can vouch for the fact that cleaning the clubhouse is serious physical exercise and the Government is absolutely right - you don’t need to spend money at a gym, just get down to some serious cleaning! Our cleaners basically have the task of cleaning all floors, sinks and WCs, wiping down windowsills, and other odds and ends, as well as topping up soap and paper in changing rooms. This work fills their allotted time, especially as wet and sandy floors are inevitable in a sailing club like ours and they take time to deal with. Having experienced what work is involved | thought it fair to remind members how they can help as we approach the club’s busiest time. After using a lounge table, please use the bins to avoid leaving any litter on tables and floor, and wipe your table down before you leave so it is clean for the next user. Aim to leave the changing rooms as clean and tidy as possible, taking your property home with you and using bins for any litter - it takes time to pick up bits of damp paper from a wet floor. Members who use the tea bar, please take a couple of minutes to wash up properly, dry and put away all crockery and cutlery you have used, at the time of writing this, the draining board is nearly full! This task won’t be added to the cleaner’s workload as it is expected that the users or any occasional volunteer will between them keep the tea bar in a reasonable condition. We are still very much a self-help club, run by the members for the members in order to keep costs down, and we can all make the environment a pleasant one for ourselves and others by all making just a small effort. Maureen Ball

Letters & Articles J.E.Pateman CBE. Jack Pateman, who died on the 28th August, was managing Director of Marconi Avionics. He was President of the Marconi Sailing Club for several years. His sloop, "Oenanthe", regularly cruised in France, Holland and our East Coast. He led the annual visit to our club to support dinghy races between his Rochester team and our club. He liked to recount how, after leaving a Laying-Up supper at the Lion & Lamb, he was fined for driving the wrong way down Duke Street! MSC AGM Minutes 2003 Minutes of the Thirslet Sailing Club Ltd Annual General Meeting held at the MASC Beehive Lane Chelmsford on the i November 2003 1 Apologies for absence: Apologies for absence were received from M Willis; D Kirby; J Todds; G Preston; C Anderson; D Burrow; K Starkie; P Tovey. 2 Previous Minutes: None to consider. 3 Matters arising: None 4 Commodores Report: The Commodore, Mr N T Pembleton, presented his report, see attached. Questions: None Acceptance of the report was proposed by H Griffiths and seconded by M Smith and accepted unanimously by those present. 5 The Honorary Secretaries Report.

The Honorary Secretary, Mr P D Black, presented his report in which he commented upon: e Membership e Club Insurance e Committee Meetings Questions. None Acceptance of the report was proposed by M Bates, seconded by C R Davies and accepted unanimously by those present. 6 The Honorary Treasurers Report. The Honorary Treasurer, Mr J Bird, presented his report. Questions. Mr D Carmichael asked how much the club borrowed to purchase the site and at what interest rate. Mr J Bird replied that the sum borrowed is £221,900 at a variable interest rate currently at six percent. Mr M Sisson suggested that it might have been cheaper to borrow money from the membership. Mr Bird in reply said that when all the details are taken into account the bank offers the best deal. Acceptance of the report was proposed by S Elwell, seconded by F Bennett and accepted unanimously by those present. 7 Sailing Secretaries Report. The Sailing Secretary, Mr D Williams, presented his report, see attached. Questions. None Acceptance of the report was proposed by R Greygoose, seconded by M Hellewell and accepted unanimously by those present. 8 Proposals. 8.1 Resolution 1. Amendments to the membership fees and payments. Proposed by the Management Committee. Questions. Miss J Ball requested clarification on the summer storage fees for trailers, how would this impact on catamaran trailers and boxes? Mr N Pembleton explained that charges would not be attracted towards trailers associated with a boat enjoying a paid up Boat Permit Fee. Mr R Mander noted that his fees for 2004 had uplifted by twenty nine percent and asked if this was likely to be the normal increase in future years, Mr Bird replied that this would not be the case. Miss J Ball commented that our fees now closely reflected that of other clubs on the river and may have an adverse effect upon our membership recruitment. Mr R Davis asked for an explanation of the membership class “Senior Life Member’, Mr N Pembleton explained. Acceptance of the report was proposed by P Sayer, seconded by F Bennett and accepted unanimously by those present. 8.2 Resolution 2. Selection of the New Club Name. The membership was asked to vote on three candidate names viz. Marconi Sailing Club, Thirslet Sailing Club and Stansgate Abbey Sailing Club. Voting by ballot was as follows: Marconi Sailing Club 51 votes Thirslet Sailing Club 3 votes Stansgate Abbey Sailing Club 41 votes The will now operate as Thirslet Sailing Club trading as Marconi Sailing Club until the new name can be registered. 8.3 Resolutions 3,4 and 5. Election of officers Proposed by the Management Committee. President Tony Benn Carried with two against Vice Presidents P Bloomfield and S Glynn Carried Executive Officers C R Davies, P Clayton, R Ball, C E Davies, C Shenton and J Bird. Carried 8.4 Resolution 6. Election of the Management Committee Names taken as a block Carried Any other Business. Mr R Greygoose on behalf of the RNLI thanked the members and the club for donations and contributions. Mr D Ball reminded members that the annual RNLI rowing race would take place at Maldon on Boxing Day 2003. Mr C R Davies thanked the club on behalf of the Cirdan Sailing Trust; money raised for he trust by the East Coast Piers Race this year totalled £9485. Mr C Davies then thanked the retiring members of the Management Committee, Mr F Bennett, Mr R Godbold and Mr D Kirby. Finally he paid tribute to Mr N Pembleton for his crucial role in the site purchase “the right man at the right time”. In response Mr Pembleton said he could have achieved nothing without the wholehearted support of the club. Mr K Coleman, an active member of the Cirdan Sailing Trust, thanked the club on behalf of the Trust. Mr N Pembleton presented two awards. First the seamanship trophy to cadet Nick Miller for his part in rescuing a dismasted dinghy and the crew and secondly Bob and Elsie Anderson received the Commodores Plate for their loving care of the gardens at Stansgate, an inspiration and joy to us all. There being no further business the meeting closed at 1200hrs.

Page 7 Commodore’s Report for the Club AGM 2004 The first thing to say is that this report does not set out to name names. I do not intend to use this report to record all the thanks that are due to the many people who take special responsibility for the operation of the club. The need to give those thanks is great but it will happen elsewhere. My task here is to provide some information that is required by statute (under the Companies Act) and to give members a summary of our management activities during the past year alongside an indication of our intentions for the coming year. I am required to confirm that our principle activity during the past year has continued to be the provision of sailing facilities to our membership. Our management structure as a limited company is not dissimilar to that which applied previously. The Board or Executive now, of course, assumes ultimate responsibility for the club operation – rather than MASC as was previously the case– and was strengthened to allow for the additional workload. The board comprised six directors:  Ray Ball  John Bird (Finance)  Peter Clayton  Chris Davies (Managing)  Claire Davies  Clive Shenton All of whom have specific operational responsibilities as Flag Officers of the Club. The board appoints an Honorary Secretary and during the past year that post was held by Patrick Black. The board met formally each month since the last AGM and has conducted such other meetings of sub-groups as have been appropriate from time to time. The Management Committee, which also meets monthly, continues to provide a forum in which representatives of all aspects of the club can share and discuss matters relating to the day to day operation of the site and activities. Then there is a network of sub-committees that deal with specific areas of activity, who report their activities and recommendations through the Management Committee. These various committees provide the formal focus for all our discussions but a lot of work is done informally either face-to-face or by electronic means. I am required to mention here any political or charitable donations made during the year. I am proud of our ongoing work in support of the Cirdan Sailing Trust and can confirm that, through ECPR, we were able to donate £9400 to that charity. We also donated £450 to RNLI and £50 to St Johns. However, all these sums were raised during events and were not paid from club income Our focus during 2004 had three elements – to better understand our operations and how we manage them, to tidy up our presentation of the site and to focus on sailing activity. It has been and was intended to be a cautious approach both in practical and financial terms. We were concerned to understand fully the implications of our change of status for the way we managed ourselves and clear that consolidation of and confidence in what we have now is an essential pre-requisite to any decisions about future development. We have achieved a great deal – but, I suppose inevitably, live with the frustration of things not achieved or not completed. Dealing with the positives in no particular order:  We have maintained and developed a strong Social Calendar. We have had some excellent events, all of which were well supported.  We have had a full and varied sailing calendar with some innovation.  Introduced a devolved system of budgetary responsibility and control.  Maintained and extended the range of Open events held here.  Our sailors have been active on the circuits on a worldwide basis.  We have created one of the most modern websites in the sailing club world.  We have increased our level of membership. Open day was a great success, cadet numbers are at a record level, and we have a greatly increased number of windsurfers.  We have continued to improve equipment in cause of safety, efficiency, convenience and cost control.  We have made some cautious but significant improvements to the site. We removed the lake and the hump, undertook repairs to the hard, greatly improved the Dell Bar, re-tiled the Womens’ showers and provided new wash basins there also. We will continue during 2005 to develop on these achievements and to tackle new opportunities to ensure that the club functions smoothly within the limits of our financial and physical resources. It has not always been straightforward and one significant issue we have had to deal with is that of succession in the numerous voluntary posts that are part and parcel of life in a club like this one. Turnover can be healthy but, at the same time continuity is desirable. We have to acknowledge and respect the need for some (perhaps most) people to be able to commit themselves for a limited time and then bow out – but we also have to build mechanisms to enable us to cope with and benefit from those changes – rather than be penalised by them. We will continue to work on ways of making our succession planning more effective and less stressful. This leads me neatly into the slightly wider issue of duties and self-help. Issues that at times cause us some confusion and even heartache. Dealing with the question of duties first of all – this Club is no different from 1000 others in that it can only function with the direct support and co-operation of its membership. Sharing responsibility for Support Boat duties, Race Officer Duties, OOD duties and basic housekeeping is a feature of life for the majority of sailing clubs in the land – only the well heeled, highly expensive and therefore exclusive clubs can lay on sufficient paid support to enable members to avoid these responsibilities completely. Of course, we employ a cleaner and we may find in the fullness of time that we can employ other people to undertake some of the routine maintenance and administration of the club – but we will not be able to escape the

Page 8 need for member’s involvement in all the key operational areas. Members must recognise this and be prepared to do their bit. We will manage the rotas but we rely on individual support and will take a dim view (on behalf of all members) when that support is deliberately withheld. The self-help ethos is a strong feature of our make up and a feature of which many of us are proud. It is an approach that reflects the history of the club and is driven by two key elements:  It attracts a certain type of member and is therefore self-perpetuating.  The nature of our exposed cruiser moorings lends itself best to an owner-driven approach to provision and maintenance and attracts owners who tend to be self-sufficient, practical and financially cautious. These owners comprise a significant proportion of the Club membership. Self-help can be a great strength and has often enabled us to do more than we might otherwise have been able to achieve. But there are two problems that it can cause:  From time to time there is a risk of division caused by a failure to acknowledge that not everybody has the ability or inclination to be involved in every aspect or every instance of self-help activity. This can be managed so long as we are aware of it and so long as we understand the difference between self-help projects and routine housekeeping.  Too great a reliance on self-help can cause delays and compromise that work against our best interests. Maintenance and major works often require speed of action and quality assurance. It is sometimes best to use tradesmen and contractors – although there is then a corresponding need for management activity to be undertaken by members. We will continue to manage this situation to achieve the best possible results. In summary we have adopted a cautious approach to our first year of financial independence and this is reflected in the figures already circulated to you. That cautious approach will continue into next year. We will continue to test and enhance our financial controls; we will continue to test and refine our operational structure and systems; and we will continue with our programme of protecting our investment of our facilities. There will be greater emphasis, however, on looking forward to what we want to achieve for ourselves in the years ahead and in laying the groundwork for future decisions about how we might improve our facilities and our operation. I would like to close by thanking the whole membership for their support of the Board during the last year and inviting anybody with any comments on what we do or what we hope to do to contact me or any board member now or at any time. Page 10 Minutes rd of The Handicap Fleet AGM 2004 3 December 2004 at 20:00 1. Apologies. Martin Brooks, Jon Kidd, Angela Aries, Fenella Thomas, Clive Shenton 2. Racing Review 2004 • Kate Williams presented a brief analysis of race turnouts for the 2004 season. • The extraction of separate morning and afternoon results to generate am and pm series results was not felt to be a success. The aim had been to support and encourage racers who generally could only make one race on a given Sunday by giving them a fighting chance of a good series result. In the event, most sailors made all or none of the races on a given day. Morning and afternoon results were generally identical to those for the overall series. It was felt that the additional work for the results secretary was not justified. 3. Racing Programme for 2005 • The am/pm series will not be repeated in 2005, but a number of new features to the 2005 racing programme were discussed: o The Summer Points series will now be split in two, giving an Early Summer and a Late Summer series. This should lessen the number of people forced to count one or more DNC (Did Not Compete) scores in their series result due to summer holiday absences. o The first racing Sunday of the year will be a designated shakedown, with rigging time in the morning, and single race in the afternoon. o The last racing Sunday of the year will be a designated final fling, with a single race in the morning, and de-rigging, de-masting and trailer loading time in the afternoon. • Various ideas were discussed to build on racing turnout. These included: o Plan and advertise in the year book one ot two “Racing for beginners” days. These should be held on normal points racing Sundays. One or more fleet representatives would be designated to meet, greet and show the ropes to members who would like to try racing, but need some pointers to get started. o Lunchtime reps could be designated, especially in the high summer to talk with less frequent/experienced club racers between races, to discuss courses, conditions, weather, boats or anything else helpful. o Make special efforts to publicise one-off races. o Use all available methods of communication to engage fleet members (website, Navigans, email, noticeboards, etc). ACTION – Fleet Captain to put ideas into practice in 2005! 4. Cruising • Two cruising events were held in 2004. The first, an up-river cruise to Maldon, was organised by Dave Williams and well supported. The latter down-river cruise was less well supported, and curtailed by an absence of wind. • In an endeavour to build on the partial success of 2004, two cruising events were also agreed for 2005: th o 28 May 2005 - Down River Cruise (e.g. Mersea or Bradwell) – High Tide 17:02 th o 20 August – Up River Cruise (e.g. Maldon, Mayland or Heybridge) – High Tide 13:58 • It was agreed that, subject to club management approval and levy of a small fee, more cruising classes should be invited and encouraged to visit MSC. This would help to raise the club profile within classes, and put more club members get more involved with their class associations. ACTION - All to Consider contacting cruising sections of our own class associations with a view to setting dates in 2006. • The idea of self-organised “class days” was muted. Some types of boat (GP14, Wanderer, Laser, etc) are well supported within the handicap fleet. Cruising, racing or social events organised by owners of specific classes could encourage more people to sail and build new friendships. ACTION – Fleet Captain to assist organisers of these events to contact boat owners via the membership list. 5. Dinghy Park The layout and general use of the dinghy park was discussed. Suggestions for 2005 included: • Consider removing the gangway which runs through the dinghy park toward the club house door and utilise this space to park dinghies. All boats could use the club roadway to access the hard as the large handicap fleet boats already do. • Use the actual count of boats in each size taken in 2004 as the basis of the dinghy park layout in 2005, rather than the membership boat list, which is not complete at the time the dinghy park layout is set. Spaces for larger boats were in especially short supply in 2004. • Police the positioning of ‘large’ and ‘medium’ handicap boats, to ensure they park in the right areas, and within the marked bays. • Number spaces in each row consecutively (A1,A2,A3,A4,A5…), rather than having odd numbering/even numbering for alternate rows. • Make more noticeboard space provision in the club house to enable dinghy park plans and instructions to be fully displayed and more easily maintained. • The club could consider supplying suitable ground anchors (at a cost) for dinghy owners who do not have the means to secure their boats. ACTION – Fleet Captain to liase with the dinghy park coordinator. 6. Report from the Rear Commodore

Page 11 Claire Davies updated the AGM on a number issues and initiatives: th th • On the 11 and 12 of June, the Byte class nationals are coming to MSC. This is a popular class amongst our younger sailors, and we can expect a good turnout from members and visitors. This will coincide with camping and the club Summer Ball social. • Claire is continuing to investigate ways in which the club might be able to offer and fund club boats for use by all members. Options include leasing or fleet purchase & buy back agreements with major dinghy manufacturers. Its early days yet and the case for more club boats has yet to be proved. • The sailing sub committee would like to introduce at least one additional fixed race mark for 2005. This would give Race Officers more flexibility in setting courses. Claire is in discussion with the river bailiff regarding acceptable sites. 7. Election of Fleet Captain David Ball was unanimously re-elected as fleet captain. 8. AOB • It was noted that the hard had been especially slippery at times this year. Claire confirmed that scrubbing had taken place. It was felt that is more dinghy sailors were qualified to drive club tractors, scrubbing could be undertaken more frequently. New concrete chocolate blocks are now being manufactured to improve grip at smooth concrete sections. • It was noted that the Jack B did not always appear to have a pair of binoculars on board. Claire Davies confirmed that equipment would be checked as part of the planned review of support boat code-of-practice documents this winter. • The level of support boat cover at certain events was discussed. The club’s own guidelines in general require a ratio of 1 support boat to 20 competing dinghies or catamarans.

Sail to end of information, call Frank on Frank Burgess A View From The Rear Well, here we are at the beginning of another sailing season. You will have received your yearbooks by now and seen the programme, but we are ringing the changes right at the start of the season. Nothing radical, just tweaks, I promise! The first race of the season will be a one-off event, the early season equivalent of the final fling. It will be a single, all-in handicap race, with a late start after a spot of communal boat-moving and -rigging and some warming brunch from the galley. Our early Easter this year was an opportunity to look at the Bank Holiday series, which always has plenty of entries but not many real contenders as so many of us go away for the Bank Holidays. So we have removed one from the equation, racing instead for Easter Eggs over the second weekend of racing. A few more 'tweaks' to come as the season progresses, which we hope you will agree improves rather than detracts from the quality of our Sunday Sailing programme. Not all our dinghy sailors race: some don't like to, some can't make Sundays, some have never raced. For that last group of sailors, the handicap fleet will be laying on a couple of 'racing for beginners' events during the season. These will be an informal opportunity to join some seasoned racers observing the activities and learning the basics from the shore before trying it on the water. Please can I remind all of you who volunteered on your renewals to support club sailing in support boats or in the race box to check the rotas. They are all here in this Navigans, and will shortly be on the website too, as is the programme. Please make sure that you put the date in your diaries as soon as possible. Without your valuable support we cannot put on the varied programme to which we aspire. Finally, on a more personal note, I should let you know that, due to a change of job, I will be moving away from the area and will have to stand down as Rear Commodore. I am very grateful to Clive Shenton for agreeing to a change of 'portfolio' mid-term to take back the sailing agenda he thought he had left behind. I am not disappearing immediately, and will continue the duties until I have to give up. I will be around regularly for the early season, and you can't get rid of me that easily anyway! Happy sailing - I look forward to seeing you on the water. Claire Davies Rear Commodore (Sailing) Keep up to date at the MSC web site www.marconi-sc.org.uk Username: [redacted] Password:stansgate27
